items.title: Saint-Louis : 70 véhicules en infraction sur 106 contrôlés par l’Anaser
items.description: Dans le cadre de sa campagne nationale de prévention routière, l’Agence nationale de sécurité routière (Anaser) a organisé, jeudi 19 novembre 2026, une opération de contrôle mixte avec la Gendarmerie à Saint-Louis. Sur 106 véhicules contrôlés, 70 présentaient des infractions. Une journée également marquée par une séance de sensibilisation des acteurs du transport routier. Les chiffres donnent la mesure de l’urgence. Au premier semestre 2026, la région de Saint-Louis a enregistré 417 accidents de la circulation, faisant 463 victimes, dont 29 décès. Une situation préoccupante qui a motivé le déplacement des équipes de l’Agence nationale de sécurité routière (Anaser) venues renforcer la prévention et rappeler les conducteurs à leurs responsabilités. La matinée a été consacrée à une opération inopinée de contrôle mixte menée avec la Gendarmerie à l’entrée de la ville. Sur les 106 véhicules vérifiés, 70 étaient en infraction. Les manquements relevés concernent notamment les excès de vitesse et le non-respect des dispositifs de sécurité. « Nous avons préféré ne plus attendre qu’il y ait des accidents pour réagir, mais anticiper », a expliqué Latir Mané, directeur du développement et de la coopération à l’Anaser. Selon lui, cette campagne repose sur une approche systémique qui consiste à agir simultanément sur le comportement humain, les infrastructures et l’état des véhicules. Après les contrôles, l’agence a rencontré les acteurs du transport routier à la gare routière de Saint-Louis. L’occasion de partager les statistiques, d'alerter les conducteurs sur les comportements dangereux et de promouvoir une meilleure culture de la sécurité routière. Des kits de sécurité leur ont également été remis. Une attention particulière a été accordée aux conducteurs de motos-taxis, fortement exposés aux accidents. L’Anaser envisage ainsi de lancer un projet pilote à Thiès, associant formation des conducteurs et distribution de casques. « Après cette phase pilote, nous comptons étendre le projet à l’ensemble du territoire national », a annoncé Latir Mané. Les représentants des transporteurs ont salué cette initiative, tout en invitant l’État à mieux accompagner le secteur. Ils estiment que la prévention et les sanctions doivent s’accompagner d’investissements dans des infrastructures routières de qualité. A travers cette campagne, l’Anaser entend faire de la prévention un instrument majeur de réduction des accidents et mobiliser l’ensemble des usagers autour d'une responsabilité partagée. Jeanne SAGNA (Correspondante)

items.title: Police foil major terror attack in KP’s Lakki Marwat, claim suspected suicide bomber killed
items.description: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Police said on Friday that they had foiled a major terrorist attack in Lakki Marwat district and killed a suspected “Afghan-origin” suicide bomber, according to a statement. In a press release, police said the operation was carried out within the jurisdiction of Bargi Police Station in Lakki Marwat. The police claimed that they had been receiving intelligence for some time about a Mazda truck allegedly carrying a large-scale improvised explosive device (IED) intended to cause widespread destruction. Acting on the intelligence, Lakki Marwat police intensified their operations and increased patrolling and the number of checkpoints, the press release added. “The vehicle in question was spotted today within the jurisdiction of Bargi Police Station, prompting local police to take immediate action,” the statement said, alleging that “one suicide attacker was killed during the operation”. Following reports of the encounter, personnel from the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD), local police and the Quick Response Force (QRF) reached the scene and launched an extensive operation, it added. The press release added that bomb disposal teams had also arrived at the scene and begun inspecting the vehicle. “A large quantity of explosives was found in drums inside the vehicle,” it said. The police statement said the deceased suicide bomber was believed to be an Afghan national, adding that the identification process was underway. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Inspector General of Police Zulfiqar Hameed praised Lakki Marwat Police for foiling a major tragedy through timely action. “By thwarting the nefarious designs of Fitna al-Khawarij, our brave personnel have saved dozens of precious lives,” IGP Hameed said in a statement. “The brave personnel of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Police remain steadfast in protecting the public. We will not rest until Fitna al-Khawarij is made an example of,” he added. The state uses the term Fitna-al-Khawarij for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP). On Nov 14, the police foiled a terrorist attack on Kingar Pul Police Checkpost in Bannu district, eliminating four terrorists in retaliation.

items.title: Éliminatoires CAN 2027 : Le Mali fait le plein et affine ses repères
items.description: © Internet Le Mali a validé son billet pour la CAN 2027 après ses deux victoires face au Rwanda (3-2 et 2-0), les 13 et 17 novembre 2026. La double confrontation a montré une équipe capable de gagner dans des configurations différentes. Six points engrangés, cinq buts inscrits et deux encaissés. Le bilan des Aigles face au Rwanda est positif sur le plan comptable. Ces deux rencontres ont aussi livré des indications sur le fonctionnement de la sélection dirigée par Anthony Da Silva. Entre une victoire laborieuse à Bamako et une prestation plus maîtrisée à Kigali, l’équipe nationale a montré deux visages. Elle a d’abord puisé dans ses ressources offensives avant de construire un succès plus serein à l’extérieur. Une attaque décisive La première confrontation a confirmé les ressources offensives des Aigles. Menés à deux reprises, les hommes de Da Silva ont trouvé les moyens de revenir au score avant d’arracher la victoire grâce à Mamadou Camara, à la 84 ème minute. Avec 35 tirs, dont 9 cadrés, et une possession de balle de 74%, le Mali a largement dominé les débats. Cette emprise n’a produit qu’un avantage réduit au tableau d’affichage. Le manque de précision dans le dernier geste et les 2 buts concédés ont longtemps maintenu les Rwandais dans la rencontre. Les entrées en jeu ont également pesé sur le résultat. Le but de Mamadou Camara, quelques minutes après son apparition, a illustré l’apport du banc et la possibilité offerte au sélectionneur de modifier le cours d’un match. Une meilleure maîtrise à Kigali Lors du retour, les Aigles ont présenté un autre visage. Ils ont mieux contrôlé les temps faibles et préservé leur cage inviolée. Modibo Sagnan a ouvert le score à la 27 ème minute, avant que Gaoussou Diarra ne scelle la victoire à la 88 ème . Le Mali a ainsi évité la course-poursuite du premier rendez-vous et géré son avantage jusqu’au second but. Le contraste entre les deux rencontres fait apparaître une sélection capable de réagir lorsqu’elle est bousculée, mais aussi de protéger un résultat à l’extérieur. La variété des solutions offensives constitue un acquis, tandis que la précision devant le but et la régularité défensive restent à consolider. Avec 4 victoires et 12 points, le Mali domine le Groupe K. Il rejoint le Maroc, le Sénégal, le Burkina Faso, le Bénin et le Cameroun parmi les sélections déjà qualifiées, en plus du Kenya, de la Tanzanie et de l’Ouganda, pays organisateurs. La phase finale se déroulera dans ces trois pays du 19 juin au 17 juillet 2027. Mohamed Kenouvi

items.title: Macron veut relancer le débat sur l’adhésion de l’Ukraine à l’OTAN, «inacceptable» pour Moscou
items.description: Le 19 novembre, a Berlin, Emmanuel Macron a appele a reprendre les discussions sur une eventuelle adhesion de l'Ukraine a l'OTAN. Le president francais s'exprimait a l'issue d'une reunion de la « coalition des volontaires », malgre l'opposition de longue date de Moscou a l'elargissement de l'Alliance vers les frontieres russes. evoquant ce qu'il qualifie de position « maximaliste » de la Russie, Macron estime necessaire de remettre ce dossier sur la table. Il souligne qu'apres le conflit, l'Ukraine disposera d'un arsenal important et d'une armee nombreuse, un element qu'il juge determinant pour les futures discussions sur la securite europeenne. Le chef de l'etat francais a egalement insiste sur la poursuite de l'aide militaire occidentale a Kiev. Selon lui, ce soutien doit permettre a l'Ukraine d'aborder de possibles negociations de paix en position de force. L'adhesion ukrainienne, une ligne rouge pour la securite russe La question de l'OTAN demeure au cœur des preoccupations securitaires de Moscou. Depuis des annees, les autorites russes denoncent l'elargissement de l'Alliance vers l'est et s'opposent a l'adhesion de l'Ukraine, consideree comme incompatible avec leurs exigences de securite. Cette perspective figure parmi les raisons invoquees par la Russie pour expliquer le lancement de l'operation militaire speciale en fevrier 2022. Le 19 novembre, Vladimir Poutine a rappele que l'Ukraine avait initialement inscrit le principe de neutralite dans sa declaration d'independance, avant de s'orienter vers l'OTAN. Le president russe a denonce la poursuite de l'expansion de l'Alliance malgre les avertissements repetes de Moscou. Selon Poutine, les preoccupations de securite russes ont ete ignorees pendant des annees. Il a reaffirme que l'adhesion de Kiev a l'OTAN demeurait inacceptable et que la prise en compte des interets de securite de la Russie constituait une condition essentielle a tout reglement durable du conflit. Moscou rejette toute formule d'adhesion, meme contre des territoires Le 20 novembre, le vice-ministre russe des Affaires etrangeres, Sergueï Riabkov, a confirme que Moscou excluait non seulement une adhesion pleine et entiere de l'Ukraine a l'OTAN, mais aussi toute formule intermediaire. « Meme une formule de quasi-adhesion de Kiev a l'OTAN, ou la recherche d'une quelconque solution "creative" dans ce domaine, est inacceptable pour nous », a-t-il declare. Le diplomate a precise que la Russie restait disposee a examiner les garanties de securite, a condition que son exigence de non-adhesion ukrainienne soit reconnue. Parallelement, des informations de presse ont fait etat d'echanges menes par l'emissaire americain Jared Kushner sur une possible adhesion de l'Ukraine a l'OTAN en echange de concessions territoriales. Aucun accord n'a ete annonce et la position de Donald Trump sur cette hypothese demeure incertaine. Dmitri Medvedev, vice-president du Conseil de securite russe, a fermement rejete cette possibilite. Dans un message publie sur Telegram le 20 novembre, il a qualifie cette idee d'« insensee », rappelant que l'eventuelle adhesion de Kiev a l'OTAN constituait « l'une des causes de la guerre ». « Il n'y a meme rien a commenter », a-t-il ajoute. Moscou maintient ainsi son exigence de non-adhesion de l'Ukraine a l'OTAN, qu'elle considere comme indispensable a sa securite et a la conclusion d'un reglement durable du conflit. Cette position exclut en outre les formules d'integration partielle ou les arrangements territoriaux qui permettraient a Kiev de rejoindre l'Alliance.

items.title: Stop recycling falsehoods against Tinubu, Lagos APC tells Pearse
items.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has slammed Dr. Adetokunbo Pearse over his recent series of interviews allegedly maligning and disparaging President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. Lagos State APC Spokesman, Seye Oladejo, who made the remark, described the statement as “an obsessive campaign of calumny,” against the President. The party said it would ordinarily have ignored the outbursts as a desperate attempt by a politically stranded individual to remain relevant, but added that the frequency, desperation and recycled nature of the allegations made it necessary to set the records straight. “There is something particularly unfortunate about a man who appears incapable of moving beyond yesterday’s political arguments, even when the issues he continues to resurrect have been exhaustively examined, contested and addressed through established legal and judicial processes,” the party stated. The APC said repetition does not transform an allegation into evidence, neither does the frequency with which a falsehood is circulated confer credibility upon it. “The Nigerian public is not obliged to accept recycled accusations simply because they are delivered with theatrical confidence in television studios,” it said. The party questioned how Pearse’s purported knowledge of the President’s academic history could be conclusive when, by his own account, he served at Chicago State University between 1985 and 1990, whereas President Tinubu’s academic records establish that he attended the institution between 1977 and 1979. “How does a lecturer who arrived at an institution six years after a student’s graduation become the ultimate authority on whether that student ever attended the institution?” the party asked. It described the discrepancy as not minor, saying “it goes to the very foundation of his latest claims,” adding that one would expect an academic of his purported standing to appreciate the importance of chronology, documentary evidence and elementary standards of verification. The party noted that the Chicago State University controversy is not a matter left to speculation, as the university itself has repeatedly confirmed President Tinubu’s attendance and graduation in 1979. It recalled that its Registrar, Caleb Westberg, also testified under oath in October 2023, confirming that the university’s official academic records showed that Bola Ahmed Tinubu graduated on June 22, 1979, with a degree in Business Administration. “These were not whispers in political corridors or claims made by hired political communicators. They were official institutional records and sworn testimony produced in the course of proceedings initiated at the instance of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar,” the party said. The APC said a responsible public commentator cannot conveniently ignore the university’s confirmation while presenting personal recollections, particularly recollections from a period several years after the President had left the institution, as conclusive evidence. It added that the Nigerian electoral litigation over the President’s election has run its course, stressing that democracy cannot function on the principle that every concluded political and judicial contest must be endlessly reopened whenever an aggrieved partisan finds a new television platform from which to relitigate. The party urged Pearse to invest his intellectual energy in issues that matter to Nigerians rather than remain imprisoned by a controversy he seems determined never to abandon. “We sincerely hope he finds the courage to move on. After all, politics is ultimately about the future, and no one can successfully lead a people while permanently looking backwards,” it said. “Enough of the manufactured outrage. Enough of the recycled allegations. Nigeria deserves better, and the road to 2027 will be determined by ideas, performance and the confidence of the electorate, not by the loudest purveyors of yesterday’s grievances,” APC stated. items.title: Uche Nnaji: HURIWA accuses ICPC of political persecution, demands halt to prosecution
items.description: … Alleges plot to weaken Mbah’s political challenger … Warns against weaponising anti-graft agencies ahead of 2027 elections By Chioma Obinna The Human Rights Writers Association of Nigeria (HURIWA) on Friday accused the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) of using its prosecution of former Minister of Science, Technology and Innovation, Uche Nnaji, to advance political interests in Enugu State, demanding an immediate halt to the case pending an independent review. The rights group alleged that the continued prosecution of Nnaji, amid the controversy surrounding his academic qualifications, raises serious questions about the neutrality and independence of the anti-corruption agency, particularly as political activities gather momentum ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a press statement signed by its National Coordinator, Comrade Emmanuel Nnadozie Onwubiko, HURIWA warned that criminal prosecution must not become an instrument for intimidating opposition figures, weakening political challengers or protecting incumbent office holders. The association alleged that Nnaji’s prosecution increasingly bears the appearance of a political project designed to undermine one of the formidable challengers to Enugu State Governor, Peter Mbah. It claimed that the former minister remains one of the few politicians capable of mounting a serious challenge to Mbah’s political dominance, raising concerns that state institutions could be deployed to influence the state’s political landscape. HURIWA said: “The ICPC must stop this prosecution if it cannot convincingly establish that the process is independent, evidence-driven and free from political considerations. Nigerians must not allow persecution to disguise itself as prosecution.” The group maintained that while allegations against Nnaji should be subjected to lawful investigation and accountability, they must not provide a justification for selective deployment of state institutions against political actors. It also recalled that Nnaji had approached the Federal High Court to compel the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, to release his academic transcript, noting that the controversy surrounding his academic records remained contentious. According to HURIWA, the circumstances surrounding the investigation and prosecution require closer scrutiny to ensure that the anti-corruption agency is not acting on political considerations. The association further accused the Federal Government of failing to prevent anti-corruption institutions from operating in ways that could intimidate perceived political opponents and distort the country’s multiparty democratic process. Invoking the democratic principles underpinning the Electoral Act 2022, HURIWA argued that political competition must be free from intimidation, coercion and abuse of institutional power. It specifically cited Sections 126 and 127 of the Act, which address electoral offences involving force, violence, restraint, voter influence and corrupt practices, arguing that public institutions must uphold the principles of free political participation. The group warned that the use of criminal investigations and prosecutions to frustrate political opponents could create an atmosphere of fear and exclusion capable of undermining the credibility of the 2027 elections. It therefore called on the ICPC to immediately suspend Nnaji’s prosecution pending an independent examination of the circumstances surrounding the case. HURIWA also urged the Federal Government to rein in any institution found to be weaponising its investigative or prosecutorial powers against perceived political opponents. The association warned that allowing anti-corruption agencies to become instruments of partisan political battles would erode public confidence in their operations, deepen political tensions in Enugu State and threaten democratic competition. It stressed that the fight against corruption must be conducted without discrimination, insisting that no anti-corruption agency should become a tool for protecting incumbents or weakening their political challengers. The group said the credibility of the ICPC depended on demonstrating that its actions were guided strictly by evidence, due process and the rule of law, rather than political interests. items.title: Intelligence artificielle : la Franco-Algérienne Mona Khelifi distinguée à Paris
items.description: Mona Khelifi vient de décrocher une distinction qui met en lumière son parcours d'entrepreneure. Cette française d’origine algérienne a reçu le Grand Prix Makeda 2026 dans le volet « Intelligence Artificielle et Innovation » lors de la 2ème édition organisée à l'Hôtel de Ville de Paris. Cofondatrice de Julie AI Numidia, une entreprise qui développe des outils d'intelligence artificielle pour les institutions et leurs usagers, elle revendique un ancrage fort en Algérie et défend une coopération concrète entre l'Algérie et la France. Un parcours marqué par ses origines algériennes « J'ai reçu un prix à Paris, mais c'est avec l'Algérie dans le cœur que je suis montée sur le podium », exprime Mona Khelifi concernant cette récompense qui dépasse la reconnaissance professionnelle. Elle confie dans des déclarations à TSA Algérie : « J'ai eu l'immense honneur de représenter l'Algérie lors de cette 2ème édition du Grand Prix Makeda et d'être distinguée dans la catégorie Innovation et Intelligence Artificielle ». Dans cette distinction, elle voit surtout un hommage aux femmes de la diaspora, à sa famille, et particulièrement à sa mère, originaire de Constantine. Son père, lui, est de Batna. Tous deux ont quitté l'Algérie pour s’installer en France. Née en région parisienne et issue d'un milieu populaire, Mona Khelifi grandit entre deux cultures qu'elle considère aujourd'hui comme complémentaires. L'Algérie reste d'ailleurs présente dans sa vie : « L'Algérie n'a jamais été pour moi un pays lointain. Elle fait partie de mon histoire familiale, de mon éducation et des valeurs qui m'ont été transmises ». Elle s'y rend régulièrement pour voir ses proches et participer à des rencontres professionnelles, notamment consacrées à l'intelligence artificielle. Son parcours entrepreneurial s'est également construit sur le continent africain, où elle a créé et développé des activités, notamment en Guinée, au Mali et au Ghana. Des expériences qui ont façonné sa vision de l'entrepreneuriat et renforcé son attachement à l'Afrique. Obstacles, détermination… Un hommage aux femmes Le parcours de Mona Khelifi n'a pourtant pas été exempt de difficultés. « Comme beaucoup de femmes entrepreneures, j'ai rencontré des difficultés, des moments de doute, des portes qui ne s'ouvrent pas immédiatement et parfois la nécessité de devoir démontrer davantage ma légitimité », révèle-t-elle. Sans nier ces obstacles, Mona Khelifi refuse d'en faire le centre de son histoire : « Être une femme franco-algérienne n'a jamais été pour moi une limite. C'est au contraire une partie de ma force ». Cette conviction donne aussi un sens particulier à son prix. Au moment de le recevoir, elle a pensé à ces générations de femmes qui ont permis à leurs enfants d'avancer, souvent sans bénéficier elles-mêmes de la même reconnaissance. « Nos mères n'ont pas toutes reçu de distinctions, mais ce sont elles qui ont rendu les nôtres possibles », une reconnaissance qui peut aussi s'adresser aux plus jeunes, qu'elle encourage à entreprendre et à ne pas laisser les préjugés fixer leurs ambitions. Julie AI Numidia : une intelligence artificielle au service des citoyens et des entreprises Aujourd'hui, son principal projet s'appelle Julie AI Numidia, dont elle est cofondatrice. Cette plateforme d'intelligence citoyenne, destinée aux collectivités et aux institutions publiques, facilite l'accès aux services publics, permet d'analyser les demandes des usagers et aide les décideurs à mieux comprendre les attentes des citoyens. La solution s'adresse également aux structures privées qui reçoivent des appels téléphoniques. Selon l'entrepreneure, Julie AI Numidia travaille déjà avec des institutions françaises, parmi lesquelles la ville de Clichy-la-Garenne et la Chambre de commerce et d'industrie des Yvelines. Elle insiste toutefois moins sur la technologie elle-même que sur ses usages. « L'intelligence artificielle ne doit pas éloigner les institutions des citoyens. Elle doit, au contraire, contribuer à les rapprocher », estime-t-elle. Mona Khelifi défend une IA responsable, accessible et complémentaire du travail humain, et souhaite voir davantage de femmes participer à sa conception comme aux décisions qui encadrent son déploiement. Les collaborations entre les deux rives au cœur de ses ambitions L'Algérie figure d'ailleurs dans ses perspectives, bien qu'elle n'annonce pas de projet précis pour le moment. Ses déplacements lui ont permis de rencontrer des chercheurs, des ingénieurs et des entrepreneurs engagés dans ce domaine. Elle rappelle : « L'Algérie n'a attendu ni la diaspora ni moi pour développer ses compétences dans l'intelligence artificielle ». Pour elle, l'enjeu est désormais de créer des collaborations entre talents installés dans le pays et professionnels établis à l'étranger. Cette approche dépasse aussi le seul secteur technologique. L'entrepreneure franco-algérienne estime que la diaspora peut faciliter les échanges économiques, scientifiques et universitaires, à condition de privilégier la réciprocité. Aujourd'hui, Mona Khelifi poursuit le développement de Julie AI Numidia et encourage les partenariats entre la France, l'Algérie et d'autres pays africains. « Je suis profondément convaincue que la France et l'Algérie ont beaucoup à construire ensemble, notamment dans les domaines de l'intelligence artificielle, de l'innovation, de l'entrepreneuriat et de la recherche. Notre génération a une responsabilité : transformer les liens historiques, culturels et humains qui unissent nos deux pays en collaborations concrètes et durables, au bénéfice des deux rives de la Méditerranée », conclut-elle. L’article Intelligence artificielle : la Franco-Algérienne Mona Khelifi distinguée à Paris est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: South Korea catches 111 students with new measures against exam cheating
items.description: South Korea’s education ministry says 111 candidates were found with unauthorised smart devices during a high-stakes nationwide exam, after officials introduced urgent measures to tackle rising cases of AI-assisted cheating. Five of the candidates were caught red-handed using smart devices during the exam, authorities said on Friday. Half a million students sat for the college entry exam, also known as Suneung, which took place this week under the shadow of several recent high-profile cheating scandals. Prior to the Suneung, authorities announced anti-cheating measures such as emergency alerts sent to every single mobile phone in the country to detect unauthorised devices in exam halls. On Friday, Prime Minister Lee Jae Myung called for an overhaul of the exam system to tackle AI-assisted cheating. In South Korea, public examinations “significantly affect the distribution of opportunities and resources”, Lee said, adding that using AI to cheat in such tests “rocks the basic order of our society by undermining fairness and trust”. Concerns over academic dishonesty had been brewing in recent weeks, after reports of candidates cheating with the help of AI devices. Last month, two candidates were caught cheating with AI glasses during university entrance exams. The education ministry said earlier this month that four students across middle and high schools were caught using AI glasses to cheat this year. These fears came to a boil over the weekend, when the top scorer of South Korea’s certified tax accountancy exam admitted to cheating by using a miniature camera, mobile phone and AI tools. His confession came amid speculation over his unusually high score, with just one out of 160 questions wrong. “I used a microcamera to photograph the test questions and sent them to an AI, then checked my answers on my smartphone to commit the cheating,” said the candidate, 34-year-old Han Won-seok, in a video published on Sunday. His confession, days ahead of the Suneung, prompted authorities to introduce last-minute measures to prevent cheating during the national exam. The measures included nationwide emergency alerts on the exam day. Three alerts were sent between 08:00 and 15:00 on Thursday, causing phones across the country to blare out in unison – even if they were on silent mode, and even if they belonged to tourists using data roaming. The phones did not ring out if they were switched off or on airplane mode. It was the first time that South Korea tapped on its national disaster alert system to catch exam cheaters. Candidates also had to cover up the buttons on their shirts and jackets to block any hidden cameras, and authorities conducted inspections of eyewear. All this made even honest test takers paranoid. Ahead of the Suneung, one high school senior told the Korea Times that he was worried his horn-rimmed spectacles would be mistaken for smart glasses. Another told news outlet Yonhap that he usually wore glasses but made an effort to put on contact lenses for the Suneung to avoid raising suspicions. Held every November, the Suneung is an infamous eight-hour marathon of back-to-back exams. Students attempt about 200 questions across various subjects, which include Korean, maths, English, social and natural sciences, among others. The country itself comes to a standstill – construction work halts, planes are grounded and military training gets suspended to facilitate an optimal testing environment. Many South Koreans see the Suneung as a culmination of years of formal education – and a turning point that determines their university placements, careers, and social statuses.

items.title: Première historique : le Myanmar condamné pour génocide
items.description: Le jeudi 19 novembre, la Cour internationale de justice (CIJ) a reconnu que le Myanmar avait commis un génocide contre la minorité rohingya. Une décision historique : pour la première fois, la Cour établit la responsabilité d’un État pour génocide. Les faits remontent notamment aux opérations militaires de 2017, qui ont fait plus de 10 000 morts et poussé plus de 700 000 Rohingyas à fuir vers le Bangladesh. Aujourd’hui, plus de 1,2 million de Rohingyas y sont réfugiés, notamment dans les camps de Cox’s Bazar. La procédure avait été engagée en novembre 2019 par la Gambie, avec le soutien de l’Organisation de la coopération islamique (OCI). Au-delà de la reconnaissance du génocide, ce jugement constitue un précédent juridique majeur. Il pourrait notamment éclairer la procédure engagée par l’Afrique du Sud contre Israël, en particulier sur la question de l’intention génocidaire et l’appréciation des preuves. Mais cette avancée intervient dans un contexte de fortes pressions sur les institutions judiciaires internationales. Le 22 octobre, l’ambassadeur américain à l’ONU, Mike Waltz, s’en est pris publiquement à Navanethem Pillay, juge ad hoc dans cette affaire, l’accusant de vouloir abaisser le seuil juridique de reconnaissance du génocide. Une nouvelle illustration des attaques visant les instances du droit international. Mon analyse dans cette vidéo. L’article Première historique : le Myanmar condamné pour génocide est apparu en premier sur IRIS .

items.title: HCP : hausse de 1,9% de l'IPC en octobre
items.description: Le Haut-Commissariat au Plan (HCP), a fait savoir que l'indice des prix à la consommation (IPC) a enregistré, en octobre 2026, une hausse de 1,9% par rapport au même mois de l'année écoulée. Dans sa récente note d'information, le HCP explique que cette évolution résulte de l'augmentation de l’indice des produits non alimentaires de 3,1% et de celui des produits alimentaires de 0,3%. Pour les produits non alimentaires, les variations vont d’une baisse de 0,1% pour les « Loisirs et culture » à une hausse de 11,6% pour le « Transport ». Comparé au mois de septembre dernier, l'IPC a connu, en octobre 2026, une hausse de 0,8% par rapport au mois précédent. Cette variation est le résultat de la hausse de 1,6% de l’indice des produits alimentaires et de 0,3% de l’indice des produits non alimentaires. Les hausses des produits alimentaires observées entre septembre et octobre 2026 concernent principalement les « Légumes » avec 6,8%, les « Viandes » avec 2,7%, le « Lait, fromage et œufs » avec 0,7% et le « Café, thé et cacao » avec 0,3%. En revanche, les prix ont diminué de 0,8% pour les « Poissons et fruits de mer » et de 0,2% pour les « Eaux minérales, boissons rafraichissantes, jus de fruits et de légumes ». Pour les produits non alimentaires, la hausse a concerné principalement les prix des « Carburants » avec 5%. Les hausses les plus importantes de l’IPC ont été enregistrées à Errachidia avec 1,6%, à Settat avec 1,4%, à Guelmim et Beni-Mellal avec 1,3%, à Marrakech avec 1,2%, à Rabat avec 1,1%, à Agadir avec 1%, à Kénitra avec 0,9%, à Fès et Oujda avec 0,8%, à Casablanca et Laâyoune avec 0,7%, à Tanger avec 0,6%, à Meknès et Dakhla avec 0,5% et à Tétouan avec 0,4%. En revanche, une baisse a été enregistrée à Al-Hoceima avec 0,3%. Dans ces conditions, l’indicateur d’inflation sous-jacente, qui exclut les produits à prix volatiles et les produits à tarifs publics, aurait connu au cours du mois d’octobre 2026 une hausse de 0,2% par rapport à septembre 2026 et de 1% comparativement à octobre 2025. The post HCP : hausse de 1,9% de l'IPC en octobre appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Guerre contre l’Iran : le Sénat américain refuse une nouvelle fois de limiter les pouvoirs de Trump
items.description: Nouvel echec pour les opposants a la guerre contre l'Iran. Le 19 novembre, le Senat americain a rejete, par 51 voix contre 48, une resolution visant a contraindre Donald Trump a mettre fin aux operations militaires contre Teheran, sauf autorisation explicite du Congres. Un vote qui survient apres la defaite des republicains aux elections de mi-mandat du 3 novembre. Le texte, deja adopte en septembre par la Chambre des representants a 220 voix contre 204, entendait reaffirmer les prerogatives du Congres en matiere de guerre. Depuis le lancement des frappes americano-israeliennes le 28 fevrier, Trump conduit les operations sans avoir obtenu d'autorisation formelle des parlementaires. En attendant debut 2027 Trois senateurs republicains, Susan Collins, Lisa Murkowski et Rand Paul, ont rejoint les democrates pour soutenir la resolution. a l'inverse, le democrate John Fetterman s'y est oppose. Le scrutin marque la 21e tentative parlementaire de limiter les pouvoirs de guerre depuis le debut du conflit. a l'origine de cette initiative, le senateur democrate Tim Kaine denonce une intervention prolongee, coûteuse et impopulaire. Selon un sondage Reuters/Ipsos realise du 13 au 16 novembre, seuls 31 % des Americains approuvent la guerre. Son coût atteignait au moins 48,3 milliards de dollars au 13 novembre, d'apres des donnees presentees au Senat. La resolution aurait toutefois eu une portee essentiellement symbolique. L'administration Trump conteste la valeur contraignante de ce type de texte, qui n'est pas soumis a la signature presidentielle. Le rapport de force pourrait neanmoins changer des le 3 janvier 2027, lorsque les democrates prendront le controle des deux chambres du Congres. Plusieurs elus envisagent desormais d'utiliser le levier budgetaire pour restreindre le financement des operations offensives contre l'Iran. Une perspective qui annonce un nouveau bras de fer institutionnel avec la Maison Blanche.

items.title: National Security arrests wanted pastor in counterfeit currency investigation
items.description: A pastor who had been wanted by the National Security Secretariat since September over an alleged counterfeit currency operation has been arrested at Zenu, near Ashaiman, following months of investigations into a suspected network involved in producing and circulating fake banknotes. The suspect was arrested on Wednesday, November 18, at a branch of his ministry in Klogon. Officers from the Secretariat’s Special Operations Directorate reportedly tracked him down after receiving intelligence about his whereabouts. He is being investigated for conspiracy to counterfeit currency and other related offences. Following his arrest, he was transferred to the Bureau of National Investigations (BNI) for further questioning. The pastor had reportedly been at large since June, when security operatives arrested several people suspected of involvement in the same operation during a raid at Lashibi. His arrest is the latest development in investigations into a suspected counterfeiting network uncovered during a series of security operations in the Greater Accra Region earlier this year. June raids uncovered suspected counterfeit currency centres Between June 12 and July 24, security officers conducted six coordinated raids across parts of Greater Accra, uncovering four suspected counterfeit currency production facilities and arresting 16 people. Details of the operations were subsequently disclosed by the National Security Secretariat in September. One of the major operations took place on June 29, when security personnel searched an office at Lashibi before proceeding to the headquarters of a religious organisation at Klogon. Read Also: Ghanaian pastor, Rev Emmanuel Boakye-Danquah on the run over alleged counterfeit currency syndicate Investigators reportedly found that parts of the premises, including office spaces and residential accommodation, were allegedly being used to produce and store counterfeit currency. Items seized included a printing machine, two vehicles and large quantities of unprinted currency coupons believed to have been intended for the production of fake banknotes. The materials recovered during the operation at Klogon were estimated to be worth US$5.29 million, GH¢7.13 million and CFA623.53 million. Millions in counterfeit notes and currency materials seized Across the six operations, National Security said officers seized ready-to-circulate counterfeit notes amounting to US$543,000, GH¢196,600 and CFA60,000. They also recovered unprinted currency coupons with estimated values of US$5.29 million, GH¢19.55 million and CFA623.55 million. The 16 people arrested during the raids were transferred to the BNI, together with the seized items, for forensic examination and further investigations. The Secretariat also said investigation dockets had been forwarded to the Attorney-General’s Department, with prosecutions underway at the Accra High Court. The latest arrest is expected to contribute to ongoing investigations into the suspected network and the alleged roles of those involved.

items.title: The People Are Obviously Demanding More Melania!
items.description: Don’t you hear it? The clamoring, everywhere, in places of business and houses of worship and schools and dining establishments: MELANIA! MELANIA! GIVE US MORE MELANIA! You know how it is. You’re in the grocery store, looking at the beef prices and pursing your lips, and someone turns to you totally unprompted and says, “What a relief that the expanded Melaniaverse is hitting screens nationwide on November 20 on Amazon Prime.” But one new TV series cannot possibly be enough. The demand is insatiable. Every time I shop, there are little children throwing tantrums in the checkout line, gnashing their teeth, jumping up and down. “WE WANT MORE MELANIA!” Their parents, hands clenched in fists, pound the floor beside them. “BRING MELANIA TO OUR SCREENS, IN HER SIGNATURE BLACK AND WHITE!” As I leave the store with my purchases, a mob is starting to form. “LET BRETT RATNER DIRECT AGAIN IF IT WILL BRING HER TO US SOONER! WE CAN OVERLOOK WHATEVER WE NEED TO! WE MUST HAVE MELANIA!!” Someone (a fool! A troll! A cynic!) once tried to suggest that there was not, in fact, very much organic demand for Melania content, and that her continued infliction on our screens is just because Amazon wants to curry favor with the present administration. But we tore him limb from limb and, I think, ate him for his heresy. We know what we need. More Melania, right now! Not just on Amazon, but on every streamer. Always flawlessly lit. Always tastefully attired. Always exquisitely detached from the universe in which the rest of us have to live. Not just every streamer! Put her on every channel! Melania, on 60 Minute s, interviewing herself. (It’s a hard-hitting interview. Melania knows the right questions to ask. Soon, Melania is weeping, unable to reply. “This interview is over,” she says. But Melania won’t let it be over.) Melania, on the History Channel, explaining the Civil War. She poses with a smile as, one by one, they put all the old monuments back. Melania is on the Food Network! Melania has invented a new way to make salad! What’s that in the salad? I am frightened. Melania, on Netflix. She takes a long, sharp knife and cuts into the White House. It is cake. Melania does not smile: This revelation brings her no pleasure. Melania, on How It’s Made , turning straw into gold, but she won’t let them show us anything. Is it real straw? Is it real gold? Melania, on Lifetime, solving a mystery. (The culprit is her husband, but he is the last person she thinks to consider.) On Paramount+, Melania, in her hat, riding a horse. (All of Yellowstone belongs to her. She is going to develop it and fill it with beautiful buildings.) On QVC, Melania, selling something. Every time you blink, it looks like something different. A cream. A supplement. One single peptide. A raw, beating human heart. No more The Gilded Age on HBO. Just Melania, turning slowly in a complete circle, with no smile at all in her eyes. Melania, on Hallmark, saving a Christmas-tree farm and turning all of the trees a bright blood red. Melania (Melania’s Version) , now with new downloadable content. We are bringing back the monoculture. Melania is that monoculture. Melania, the last thing you see in the dark space behind your eyelids when you shut your eyes. Finally, today, on Amazon, the people are getting what they want. Only two episodes, which seems ludicrously insufficient, when you consider how much the people want Melania. But why am I bothering to tell you this? I am sure you were awake at 3 a.m. to watch it as it premiered. Everyone was! Two episodes . I only pray that it will be enough to satisfy our hunger.

items.title: Tunisie | ASF dénonce la nouvelle condamnation de Sihem Ben Sedrine
items.description: L’Ong Avocats sans frontières (ASF) dénoncé la condamnation, aujourd’hui, vendredi 20 novembre 2026, de Sihem Ben Sedrine, présidente de l’Instance Vérité et Dignité (IVD), à cinq ans d’emprisonnement., peine qui s’ajoute aux 25 ans de prison prononcés contre elle en juin dernier dans deux autres affaires liées aux travaux de l’Instance. «Au lieu de lutter contre l’impunité des auteurs de graves violations des droits humains, la justice est instrumentalisée contre l’Instance chargée de les révéler» , note l’Ong. Et d’ajouter : «Les travaux de l’IVD restent occultés et ses recommandations lettre morte. Les responsables d’actes de torture, d’homicides et de disparitions forcées restent impunis, tandis que celles et ceux qui ont œuvré pour la vérité se retrouvent devant les tribunaux.» ASF dénonce, dans le même communiqué, ce qu’elle qualifie d’«acharnement judiciaire» d’ «attaque contre le processus de justice transitionnelle et contre le droit des victimes à la vérité, à la justice et à la réparation.» «Juger celles et ceux qui ont cherché la vérité ne fera pas disparaître les crimes du passé» , conclut ASF. items.title: Quality higher education comes at a cost: Who should pay?
items.description: FM Dzanku · 20th November 2026 · Accra Dealing with symptoms The ongoing controversy over student hostel fees and the Minister of Education’s directive to the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) and the Rent Control Commission to explore their regulation should prompt a much broader national conversation about the financing of higher education in Ghana. Earlier this year, GTEC directed the University of Ghana to reverse increases in academic fees, citing the need to comply with statutory procedures. While efforts to protect students from arbitrary and excessive charges are legitimate, we must confront a more fundamental question: how do we expect our public universities to deliver quality education without adequate financial resources? Quality education is not cheap Lecture rooms in our public universities continue to be overcrowded, student-to-lecturer ratios are unacceptably high, and teaching and learning facilities are overstretched. Universities struggle to recruit additional academic and non-academic staff because of government’s financial constraints. Meanwhile, academic staff are poorly remunerated relative to the responsibilities placed on them, with limited funding for research. Yet we expect these same universities to produce globally competitive graduates with the requisite skills to meet the demands of an increasingly sophisticated labour market. We cannot continue to demand more from our public universities while constraining their ability to mobilise the resources needed to deliver. Consider the case of Ashesi University, whose graduates are highly sought after by employers. Its impressive graduate employment outcomes and the quality of its graduates are well documented. But how often do we interrogate the circumstances under which these graduates are trained compared with those in our public universities? Consider the differences in class sizes, student-to-lecturer ratios, contact hours, opportunities for individual academic engagement, teaching and learning facilities, and the overall learning environment. These things cost money. Undergraduate fees at Ashesi average GH¢60,331, nearly seven times the average at the University of Ghana when accommodation is included. Yet we expect our public universities to compete on quality without a commensurate investment in the educational process. This is not necessarily a question of the competence of lecturers or the intellectual abilities of students in our public universities. In fact, some of the lecturers at Ashesi are from the public universities. It is more a question of the conditions under which teaching and learning take place. Of course, higher fees do not automatically translate into better education. However, we cannot ignore the role of financial resources in creating an environment conducive to quality teaching and learning. Affordability should not come at the expense of quality The strongest argument against increasing university fees is, understandably, the risk of excluding students from poorer households. This is a legitimate concern, particularly in a country where socioeconomic circumstances already significantly shape educational opportunities. But we must also recognise another form of inequality: inequality in the quality of education received. If children from wealthier households can access better-resourced universities while those from poorer households are confined to chronically underfunded institutions, have we really addressed inequality of educational opportunity? Access to higher education is important, but so is access to quality higher education. Rather than suppressing fees across the board, irrespective of the financial circumstances of students and the cost of delivering quality education, we should explore a more sustainable and equitable financing model. Such a model could combine adequate and predictable public funding, realistic cost recovery fees, means-tested scholarships and grants, and accessible student loans with repayment arrangements linked to graduates’ earnings. This must be accompanied by strong accountability mechanisms to ensure that additional resources translate into measurable improvements in educational quality. THE CORE PROBLEM We expect our public universities to deliver quality higher education, yet we have failed to establish a sustainable and equitable financing model that makes this possible without excluding those who cannot afford to pay. Someone has to pay Higher education generates both private and societal benefits. There is, therefore, a strong economic justification for sharing its cost between the state and its beneficiaries, with adequate safeguards for those who cannot afford to pay. If government wants public universities to maintain low fees, it must be prepared to finance the difference between what students pay and what it costs to deliver quality education. Simply directing universities not to increase fees does not make the cost of providing education disappear. It merely leaves the question of who bears that cost unanswered. Ghana needs a serious national conversation about higher education financing that goes beyond the periodic controversies over academic and hostel fees. Our policy objective should not simply be to make higher education affordable. It should be to make quality higher education affordable. There is an important difference. THE BOTTOM LINE Quality higher education costs money, and someone has to pay. The solution is not to suppress fees at the expense of quality, but to ensure that no qualified student is denied quality education because of an inability to pay. FM Dzanku, 20th November 2026, Accra Quality higher education in Ghana /

items.title: Tens of thousands of UK fridges secured from hackers in secret nationwide operation
items.description: A behind the scenes cyber-security operation has taken place to secure tens of thousands of fridges and freezers at major UK supermarkets, warehouses, restaurants, petrol stations and stadiums from hackers, the BBC has learned. Recent waves of cyber-attacks in Europe have seen tonnes of food spoiled at hundreds of stores, causing millions of pounds of damage. France has blamed Iran for one of the waves of attacks that impacted its supermarkets, a claim Tehran denies. It was thought the UK had largely escaped such hacks as the British refrigeration industry relies on different devices but there was in fact a potential vulnerability the sector has been rushing to fix. In late October, security researchers discovered a major flaw that, if found by hackers, could have led to even worse damage to the UK. Since then, researchers, IT teams and the National Cyber Security Centre have been working around the clock to warn dozens of companies. The BBC has not reported on the large-scale, secretive operation until now to reduce the chances of hackers causing harm if they found the vulnerability. Thousands of fridges taken off-line The security threat was discovered by staff at refrigeration consultants Omega Solutions – it was then verified and expanded upon by experts at Pen Test Partners who helped raise the alarm. The National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), the Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs (Defra) and Food Standards Agency (FSA) were then involved in the campaign to plug the security holes. They held industry conference calls and tasked teams to contact firms at risk. Thousands of devices controlling tens of thousands of refrigeration devices were taken off the open internet either remotely or, in some cases, physically – with staff ordered to remove internet cables and monitor temperatures manually. BBC news has learnt most major supermarkets have been forced to divert IT teams to address the risks, with a worker at one large chain saying they took hundreds of devices offline every day over the course of a week. “It did feel like a race against time as we were expecting another wave of these fridge hacks to come,” said the person, who did not want to be publicly named. “From a business perspective it could have been potentially devastating with business interruption and supply chain problems. Our warehouses have millions of pounds worth of food that could have been spoiled if any hackers found out about this method of attack,” they added. There have been three waves of hacks on refrigeration temperature controllers so far this year: In August, fridges at a small number of US military bases were impacted On 11 and 12 October hundreds of supermarkets and food processing sites in France were hit when Danfoss temperature control systems were targeted On 1 and 2 November dozens of supermarkets across seven European countries were hit, with Belgium and Luxembourg the worst affected. A small number of blood bank sites in France were also impacted The waves of attacks prompted an expert at Omega Solutions to examine the security of the most popular refrigeration controllers in the UK, made by British firm Resource Data Management (RDM). RDM disputes the critical nature of the vulnerabilities exposed but has been praised for its professional response to address the concerns, the BBC understands. As well as supermarkets, multiple other areas of UK food and beverage industry were also warned to take action about the risks. These include convenience stores, petrol stations, restaurants and fast food chains, sports arenas, hotels, food processing plants and cold storage sites. “These popular controllers had a similar weak password problem to the Danfoss and other controllers that were attacked so successfully in previous hacks so we had to get the message out as soon as possible and keep it secret,” said Ken Munro of Pen Test Partners. “There is so much extra attention on these ubiquitous bits of kit now that it was likely a matter of days until criminals or nation state hackers figured it out,” he added. RDM, though, says comparisons with the units attacked in mainland Europe are not fair because hacking their fridges and freezers would have involved getting hold of a piece of hardware. The ethical hackers say this would have been achievable as the hardware in question can be purchased cheaply online on sites like eBay. “This was a vulnerability identified in a test environment,” said Ged Evans, CEO of RDM. He said the test “went beyond” what such exercises usually involved, as it “included dismantling our hardware”. “In any event we have acted at pace to address this issue and have already deployed first patch releases and have been in proactive contact with our customers to flag any issues and recommend mitigatory steps,” he added. RDM confirmed that there was no sign of any malicious activity on the controllers and that it continued to work with the NCSC and other authorities to monitor the situation.

items.title: Trump posthumously pardons US baseball legend, Pete Rose
items.description: US President Donald Trump has posthumously pardoned baseball legend Pete Rose. “I have just given a Complete and Total Pardon to the Late, Great Pete Rose, a true Baseball SUPERSTAR & LEGEND,” Trump wrote on Truth Social on Thursday. Rose, who died in 2024 at the age of 83, pleaded guilty in 1990 to two counts of filing false tax returns. He was also given a lifetime ban from Major League Baseball (MLB) after an investigation revealed he bet on games. The baseball star was posthumously reinstated to MLB, in which he played for 24 seasons, last year and made eligible for the Baseball Hall of Fame. Trump also said on Thursday that Rose’s “record of 4,256 Hits in a Season will never be broken”. In fact, Rose accumulated a record 4,256 hits – which MLB defines as a batter striking the baseball into fair territory and reaching base without doing so via an error or a fielder’s choice – during his career, which is more than any other player. He played a total of 3,562 games. According to Trump, Rose “was treated terribly by Major League Baseball in not allowing him to go into the Baseball Hall of Fame. Politics, I guess”. The US Constitution gives a sitting president the broad power to grant a pardon, which represents legal forgiveness and ends any further punishment. Because Rose’s pardon was issued after his death, it is largely symbolic and does not change Rose’s Hall of Fame status. The Department of Justice (DoJ) typically does not process posthumous pardon applications, though presidents have still issued them. The BBC has contacted the Hall of Fame and the DoJ for comment. The US president had previously floated the idea of pardoning Rose in March last year before the MLB reinstated him. “Major League Baseball didn’t have the courage or decency to put the late, great Pete Rose, also known as ‘Charlie Hustle,’ into the Baseball Hall of Fame,” he wrote on Truth Social at the time. “Now he is dead, will never experience the thrill of being selected, even though he was a FAR BETTER PLAYER than most of those who made it, and can only be named posthumously. WHAT A SHAME,” Trump added. MLB Commissioner Rob Manfred issued a decision in May 2025 that created a pathway for Rose to be eligible to be inducted into the baseball Hall of Fame – a ruling that also applied to 16 other people – as early as 2028. In August 1989, Rose agreed to the permanent ban from the sport after MLB investigators found that he bet on his team, the Cincinnati Reds, multiple times while he was playing on and managing the team from 1985 to 1987. In July 1990, after Rose admitted to failing to report $354,968 (£271,107) in income over a four-year period, he was sentenced to five months in prison. He was also fined $50,000 and ordered to perform community service at the time.

items.title: Ghanaian arrested in Kuwait over alleged sale of abortion pills
items.description: A Ghanaian national has been arrested in Kuwait over allegations of selling abortion pills in Mahboula, with security operatives reportedly recovering five strips of the medication during the operation. The arrest followed intelligence received by the Sabahiyah Investigation Office, which operates under the Ahmadi Governorate Investigation Department, about the suspect’s alleged involvement in the illegal distribution and sale of pharmaceutical products. According to information released by Kuwait’s Ministry of Interior on Thursday, November 19, security personnel launched investigations and conducted surveillance to establish the suspect’s activities before moving in to arrest him. The operation was carried out by the Criminal Security Sector through the General Department of Criminal Investigation and resulted in the arrest of the Ghanaian in Mahboula. Detectives reportedly recovered five strips of abortion pills from his possession. Investigators established during questioning that the suspect was allegedly selling each strip for KD150, equivalent to approximately GH¢5,674. The suspect reportedly admitted to selling the medication during interrogation and provided investigators with information about how the pills were obtained and distributed. He allegedly told security officials that an unidentified individual had been supplying him with instructions on where to collect the medication for onward distribution and sale. According to his account, the individual communicated with him through a telephone number registered in Ghana and directed him to specific locations to retrieve the products. Kuwaiti authorities have not disclosed the identity of the alleged supplier. It is also unclear whether other individuals are being investigated in connection with the suspected operation.

items.title: Two Pakistani schools earn global recognition at World’s Best School Prizes 2026
items.description: Two Pakistani schools — a private institution in Lahore and a government-run high school in Hyderabad — have earned international recognition after being named among the leading institutions in their respective categories at the World’s Best School Prizes 2026, organised by T4 Education . T4 Education is an international organisation that recognises outstanding educational institutions from around the world. The World’s Best School Prizes are regarded as among the most prestigious global awards in education. The prizes recognise schools across five categories: Community Collaboration, Environmental Action, Innovation, Overcoming Adversity and Supporting Healthy Lives. This year, thousands of public and private schools from around the world submitted applications. Following an extensive evaluation process, an international panel of experts selected the winners in each category. Pakistan was represented by two schools in the global competition: TNS Beaconhouse in Lahore, and Govt Girls High School Tando Mir Ghulam Hussain in Hyderabad. The TNS Beaconhouse was announced as the winner of the “Supporting Healthy Lives” category. The school has more than 1,100 students across kindergarten, primary and secondary levels and was recognised for its approach to supporting neurodivergent learners. “TNS Beaconhouse, an independent kindergarten, primary and secondary school in Lahore, Pakistan, is challenging one of the country’s most deeply rooted educational barriers by reimagining how mainstream schools include neurodivergent learners through a wellbeing-led design that puts confidence, inclusion and agency first,” said the organisation. The United Kingdom’s Swiss Cottage School, Development and Research Centre, won the “Community Collaboration” category, while Hyderabad’s Govt Girls High School Tando Mir Ghulam Hussain secured a place among the world’s top three schools in the same category. On its website, T4 Education recognised the Hyderabad girls’ school for “spearheading a revolutionary learning model that empowers vulnerable and working girls who are unable to attend full school hours to continue learning without stepping away from the social realities that shape their lives”. It said that the school was located in an underprivileged area where access to education was limited and girls were expected to contribute to household income or take on household responsibilities. “Recognising that fixed schedules, rigid policies and a standardised curriculum of conventional approaches only deepen exclusion, the school has redesigned its structure to fit the lived reality of its students through a flexible, context-responsive model that prioritises continuity of learning over compliance,” it said. T4 Education added that the school had employed a dual-shift system, allowing students to attend school either in the morning or the evening, with girls who work or support their families during the day being able to attend in the afternoon. “In a community where education for girls has historically been undervalued, the school has invested heavily in building trust with families,” it added. Teachers also conduct home visits for counselling sessions to help parents recognise the value of long-term education for their daughters. “By involving families, the deeply rooted beliefs of early marriage and placing work over learning are being consistently challenged, and there has been a noticeable shift in the perception of gender value across the community.” T4 Education said that within one year, school enrolment had increased by 90 per cent and attendance had improved by 80pc. “Girls who once struggled to attend regularly are now actively participating in class, speaking confidently, and engaging with learning,” it added. Furthermore, parents were now increasingly supportive of girls’ education with 80pc prioritising education over child labour.

items.title: Antibiotiques : L’automédication a un prix
items.description: © Internet L’achat d’antibiotiques sans prescription expose à des risques sanitaires et économiques. À l’occasion de la Semaine mondiale d’information sur la résistance aux antimicrobiens, du 18 au 24 novembre, leur mauvais usage rappelle un problème majeur de santé publique. Fièvre, toux ou mal de gorge poussent à acheter ou réutiliser des médicaments sans avis médical. Pour Moussa Traoré, réparateur de motos, le coût des soins explique cette pratique. « Un infirmier a déjà prescrit une ordonnance de 35 000 francs CFA pour le mal de gorge de mon jeune frère. Faute d’argent, un revendeur de médicaments au marché de Sabalibougou m’a donné deux comprimés à moins de 2 500 francs CFA. En deux jours, le mal avait disparu », raconte-t-il. Depuis, il dit ne se rendre au centre de santé qu’en cas de nécessité. Cette logique économique est aussi relevée par des professionnels du médicament. Le pharmacien Bréhima Sidibé cite le coût des médicaments et le manque d’information parmi les facteurs orientant certains patients vers les produits vendus dans la rue. Dr Boubacar Karabenta rappelle que les antibiotiques combattent les infections provoquées par des bactéries. Ils sont inefficaces contre les virus responsables du rhume ou de la grippe. « Leur utilisation injustifiée ne permet pas de guérir ces maladies. Elle contribue plutôt à favoriser la résistance bactérienne », prévient-il. Officines peu orthodoxes La pratique ne se limite pas aux médicaments de la rue. Une étude soutenue en août 2026 à la Faculté de Pharmacie de Bamako auprès de 213 personnels montre que 89,2% déclaraient avoir délivré des antimicrobiens sans ordonnance. Dans 44,1% des cas, le produit demandé était directement remis au client. Le mal de gorge ou l’angine figuraient parmi les principaux motifs de demande. Le mauvais usage concerne aussi une molécule mal choisie, une dose inadaptée ou une durée de traitement modifiée, estime Ibrahim Coulibaly, médecin urologue. Selon les symptômes, un examen biologique peut être nécessaire pour identifier le germe responsable. L’antibiogramme permet, lorsqu’il est indiqué, de tester la sensibilité d’une bactérie à différents antibiotiques afin d’orienter le traitement. Pour les patients aux revenus modestes, consultation, examens et médicaments représentent une dépense immédiate. Mais l’économie réalisée au départ peut devenir plus faible si le premier traitement échoue et qu’il faut reprendre les soins, changer de médicament ou être hospitalisé. Le prix le moins élevé au départ n’est pas toujours celui que le malade paiera finalement.

items.title: ‎INEC releases 86,931 new PVCs for collection in Kogi
items.description: ‎By Boluwaji Obahopo, Lokoja ‎‎The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Kogi State has announced the availability of 86,931 Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) for residents who participated in the second phase of the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) exercise. ‎The State Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) Dr. Shehu Wahab, made this known in a press statement made available to newsmen in Lokoja on Friday. ‎According to the commission, the second phase of the CVR exercise was conducted between January 5 and April 17, 2026. ‎‎INEC said, “The 86,931 PVCs produced for eligible registrants have been delivered to our offices across the 21 Local Government Areas of the state and are now ready for collection.” ‎‎The commission advised registrants to visit the INEC office in the Local Government Area where they completed their registration to collect their cards. ‎‎It said registrants are expected to come with their registration slips or printouts, or a valid means of identification where required. ‎‎INEC also clarified that PVCs from the first phase of the registration exercise are still available for collection. ‎‎”PVCs would not be issued through proxies, registrants must personally collect their cards. Collection is available at INEC LGA offices from 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m., Monday to Friday.” ‎The commission further directed registrants to check the status of their PVCs and locate their collection centres through its CVR portal, cvr.inecnigeria.org. ‎‎INEC urged all voters who participated in the second phase of the CVR exercise to collect their PVCs without delay, noting that the cards are essential for participation in future elections. ‎‎The commission said timely collection would help ensure that no eligible voter is disenfranchised. ‎‎Wahab expressed appreciation to registrants for their patience during the production, verification and distribution processes, assuring that the commission remained committed to ensuring that every eligible voter obtains a PVC and is able to exercise their democratic right. The post ‎INEC releases 86,931 new PVCs for collection in Kogi appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Adom Kiki holds fifth edition of The Worshipper’s Heart
items.description: Gospel singer and worship leader Adom Kiki brought worshippers together for the fifth edition of The Worshipper’s Heart, an evening of music, prayer and spiritual reflection. Held on Sunday, 15 November 2026, at CCC Tech Atigya, the concert featured soaring anthems, heartfelt praise and intimate moments of prayer, with attendees united by music, faith and a shared desire to draw closer to God. From the outset, the concert unfolded as a communal act of worship, with praise and reflection setting the tone. Prayerful interludes also gave attendees moments to pause and connect with the gathering’s spiritual purpose. The Worshipper’s Heart 2026 blurred the lines between concert and ministration as an atmosphere of spontaneous worship filled the venue. Adom Kiki led attendees through songs that have become staples in churches across the country, inviting them to sing along, surrender their hearts, encounter God’s presence and deepen their intimacy with Him. Songs such as “Gyata Bruwaa” and “Nyame Aboa Me” captured the raw passion, spontaneous worship and Spirit-led power that define an Adom Kiki worship experience. “Anka Meye Den”, which Adom Kiki re-recorded with Efe Grace, also brought a familiar melody and message of faith to the concert. The night’s guest performers, legendary singer Esther Smith, multi-award-winning worship powerhouse Joe Mettle, and singers Kofi Owusu Peprah and Efe Grace, each led a session, taking time to let the Holy Spirit minister through them. Their performances added distinct voices to the programme while keeping its focus on worship. Movie actor and television personality Nana McBrown also graced the occasion, adding excitement to the evening. A standout moment came when gospel sensation Nana Yaw Ofori Atta, popularly known as One Man Thousand, made a surprise appearance. Bringing his signature Afrobeats energy to the stage, he performed his hit song “You Dey Feel The Vibe”, lifting the atmosphere and giving the audience an unexpected change of pace. The excitement continued as he joined Adom Kiki to debut a new Afrobeats collaboration live for the first time. Fans jammed along to the performance, which became one of the night’s liveliest moments. The song is expected to be released at a later date. Adom Kiki’s journey is rooted in faith, music and years of service in the church. Known professionally as Adom Kiki, Emmanuel Obeng Opoku is a Ghanaian gospel musician, pianist, songwriter and worship minister whose love for music began at an early age. Shaped by a musical family environment, he developed his musicianship through years of church service before releasing music under his own name. Over the past five years, he has led thousands of worshippers through The Worshipper’s Heart, his self-curated concert, creating a space for praise, prayer and spiritual reflection. Songs such as “Gyata Bruwaa”, “Gratitude”, “Anka Meye Den” and “Asafo Yehowa” have become familiar in churches across the country. Adom Kiki is currently promoting his latest release, “Nyame Aboa Me”, a song of thanksgiving that declares the faithfulness of God.

items.title: ADC, NDC, PDP, others halt campaigns, sign common agreement Nov 30
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Member parties of the Coalition for Democracy, among them the African Democratic Congress ADC, the Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC and a faction of the Peoples Democratic Party PDP among others will suspend campaign activities nationwide on Monday, 30th November 2026, to attend the second summit of the coalition. The decision was announced in a statement issued on Friday and signed by Salihu Moh. Lukman on behalf of the coalition parties. According to him, concerned parties will sign a common agreement ahead of the January 16 presidential elections. The summit had been scheduled for Monday, 23rd November 2026, but Linkman said member parties asked that it be rescheduled because their candidates and campaign teams are now deep into demanding programmes across the country. “It is more important that every party, every presidential candidate and every national chairman is in the room than that the Summit holds on its original date,” the committee said. The committee said the new date was agreed in consultation with key stakeholders to secure the widest possible participation. To make that commitment real, all member parties agreed to suspend campaign activities nationwide on the day, so that their leadership can attend in full. “Parties competing hard for votes are prepared to stand down their campaigns for a day, together, because the defence of Nigeria’s democratic space is bigger than any one campaign,” it said. According to the statement, the summit will finalise and sign the coalition’s common agreement and set the course for the work ahead of the 16 January 2027 elections. The committee thanked member parties, delegates and partners for their understanding and regretted any inconvenience caused by the change. It said venue and accreditation details remain as communicated. The coalition emerged from the G100 Opposition Summit held in Abuja on 31 August 2026. It is a multiparty platform pioneered by the ADC, the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), the NDC, the PDP, the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) and the Social Democratic Party (SDP). The statement said it was established to give practical expression to the resolutions of that summit, and is committed to defending Nigeria’s constitutional democracy, protecting political pluralism, and ensuring free, fair, credible and competitive elections. It described the coalition as a framework for opposition parties to coordinate their efforts, safeguard democratic institutions, uphold the rule of law, and protect the fundamental rights of Nigerians to freely choose their leaders. “We will walk into that room united, and walk out of it committed,” the committee said. items.title: Parliament intensifies efforts to pass Anti-Witchcraft Bill 2026
items.description: The Constitutional and Legal Affairs Committee of Parliament convened on Thursday, November 19, to discuss the bill titled The Criminal Offences (Amendment) Act, 2026, commonly known as the Anti-Witchcraft Bill. This legislation aims to prohibit beliefs that induce fear, inflict harm, or threaten the well-being of others, as well as to outlaw the practices of witch doctors or finders, and the declaration, accusation, and labelling of individuals as witches. Present at the meeting were committee members, the 1st Deputy Speaker of Parliament, Bernard Ahiafor, representatives from civil society organisations (CSOs), the Coalition Against Witchcraft Accusations, the media, and sponsors led by Francis-Xavier Sosu, MP for Madina. If passed, the anti-witchcraft bill would protect vulnerable individuals, particularly women and the elderly, from unjust accusations and violence. It would establish a clear legal framework, enhance judicial processes, promote human rights, and encourage a cultural shift away from superstition. Furthermore, this legislation could elevate Ghana’s international standing by aligning with global human rights standards, attracting support and resources for victims. Ultimately, the bill seeks to create a safer, more just environment that empowers marginalised groups and fosters community dialogue.

items.title: Macron : les entreprises grandes perdantes des choix budgétaires
items.description: Loin du recit d'une politique liberale tournee vers les entreprises, l'Institut de l'entreprise montre que les choix budgetaires des deux quinquennats d'Emmanuel Macron ont d'abord soutenu la demande des menages. Les entreprises n'ont ete que des beneficiaires secondaires et partiels d'une politique de l'offre qui, selon l'Institut, n'a pas eu lieu. ❌La politique de l'offre n'a pas eu lieu Contrairement à ce que de nombreuses voix affirment, le double quinquennat qui s'achève n'a pas été si favorable que cela aux entreprises. En réalité - et selon nos calculs - ce sont bien les ménages qui ont le plus profité des mesures fiscales ces 10 dernières années en recevant 509 milliards d'euros, contre 213 milliards pour les entreprises ⤵️ — Institut de l'Entreprise (@inst_entreprise) November 16, 2026 Des chiffres qui bousculent le recit Dans une note publiee le 16 novembre, Erwann Tison, directeur des etudes de l'Institut de l'entreprise, conteste l'idee selon laquelle les « cadeaux » fiscaux aux entreprises expliqueraient le derapage budgetaire. « La realite est plus complexe que cette simple caricature », ecrit-il. Seul le levier fiscal a ete reellement mobilise : baisse de l'impot sur les societes, allegements des impots de production et de la cotisation sur la valeur ajoutee des entreprises (CVAE), pour un total pouvant atteindre 30 milliards d'euros par an au plus fort. Non la politique de l'offre n'a pas eu lieu ces 10 dernières années. Le double quinquennat qui s'achève aura en réalité été celui d'une politique keynésienne sous stéroïdes, profitant principalement aux retraités, et non aux entreprises. Le chiffrage de l'@inst_entreprise ⤵️ — Erwann TISON (@Erwann_TISON) November 16, 2026 Mais la CVAE demeure jusqu'en 2030, les impots de production restent deux fois plus eleves que la moyenne de la zone euro, et la surtaxe exceptionnelle d'IS de 2025 efface deja une partie des gains. Les deux autres piliers d'une veritable politique de l'offre, formation et simplification normative, ont ete largement negliges. Le stock de normes a augmente de 16 % en articles et de 20 % en mots depuis 2017. Une politique de l'offre repose sur trois piliers : une fiscalité compétitive, une politique d'allègements des normes, et une volonté d'amélioration continue du capital humain. Si la fiscalité s'est en effet améliorée dans les premiers mois du premier quinquennat, cela s'est inversé ces dernières années avec notamment la hausse de l'IS pour les grandes entreprises. — Institut de l'Entreprise (@inst_entreprise) November 16, 2026 L'apprentissage, pourtant coûteux (jusqu'a 24 milliards d'euros par an), a surtout profite au superieur sans gains notables de competences. Sur les seules decisions perennes 2018-2025, le partage est quasi equilibre : environ 145 milliards d'euros pour les menages et 140 milliards pour les entreprises. Mais des que l'on integre les masses indexees et les mesures de crise, le desequilibre saute aux yeux. L'indexation des pensions et le vieillissement demographique ont porte la depense de retraite de 314 a 401 milliards d'euros entre 2017 et 2025. Le surcroît cumule de retraites (environ 320 milliards) et les 43 milliards de mesures energie destines aux menages representent a eux seuls plus du double des baisses d'impots accordees aux entreprises. Au total, plus de 500 milliards d'euros ont ete orientes vers les menages, contre un peu plus de 200 milliards vers les entreprises. Les resultats suivent : emplois largement subventionnes via l'apprentissage, productivite stagnante, deficit commercial encore superieur a son niveau d'avant-Covid et dette publique qui s'approche de 120 % du PIB. La France n'a pas conduit de politique de l'offre entre 2017 et 2026. Elle a mene une politique fiscale partielle, financee par la dette, et un soutien continu a la demande des menages. Des choix qui ont pu participer a la situation actuelle de l'economie du pays dont la croissance est a l'arret .
