items.title: ESUT to be renamed after Jim Nwobodo – Mbah
items.description: Governor of Enugu State, Dr. Peter Mbah, has unveiled plans to rename the Enugu State University of Science and Technology (ESUT) after a Second Republic Governor of old Anambra State, Senator Jim Nwobodo, subject to stakeholders engagement and legislative due process. Mbah made this known during the 3rd Distinguished Personality Lecture of the university delivered by Nwobodo at the Barr. Peter Ndubuisi Mbah Multipurpose Auditorium, ESUT, Enugu, on Thursday. He said the idea, which was first suggested by the ESUT Alumni Association, was in tandem with his thoughts, describing it as a fitting tribute to the elder statesman, who founded the institution in 1980. The Governor emphasised that the brainchild of the ex-governor had played a critical role in the human capital development of not just Enugu State, but also the old Anambra State and Nigeria as a whole. “Recently, representatives of the alumni of this university and its associated institutions came to see me. “They asked that Enugu State University of Science and Technology be renamed in honour of Senator Jim Ifeanyichukwu Nwobodo. “I told them that I support the proposal. I was particularly encouraged that the request came from the alumni who understand, through their own experience, what the university has meant to people’s lives. “There is a legal process to follow. ESUT was established by law, and changing its name would require the appropriate legislative steps and engagement with relevant stakeholders. “I intend to begin those engagements and work with the institutions concerned to advance the proposal through the proper process. “Your Excellency, I hope that gives you some sense of the regard in which your contribution continues to be held.” The Governor praised Nwobodo’s vision and courage in leadership, especially for investing heavily in human capital development, taking the bold step to establish ESUT a few years after the civil war, not minding the enormity of the challenges involved. “I have often wondered what it must have felt like to be governor in 1979. Nigeria had just returned to civilian government after thirteen years of military rule. “The Civil War had ended less than a decade earlier, and the country was still dealing with its consequences. There was much to rebuild, and enormous pressure on the resources available to government. “For many families, university education remained beyond their reach. And here was a young governor, who decided that his state should establish a university of science and technology. “People questioned whether it could be done. Was there enough money? Could a state government sustain such an institution? Shouldn’t this be left to the federal government? “These were reasonable questions. I suspect some of them would have kept you awake at night. “But for Jim Nwobodo, the fact that a problem is difficult does not mean we can afford to avoid it. “In July 1980, Anambra State University of Technology was established. Forty-six years later, we are gathered in one of the institutions that grew from that decision. And generations of young people have gained opportunities that might otherwise have been beyond their reach,” he stated. Mbah noted that beyond the establishment of ESUT, the Nwobodo Administration encouraged communities to build schools, with government providing teachers and other support. “He also invested in industry, seeking to create employment and strengthen the state’s productive capacity. “Some of those industries later fell into decline, and today we are working to bring a number of them back into use. “The value of such decisions is ultimately found in people’s lives. A child who could attend school in their own community. A young person who became the first in their family to enter university. A household supported by employment in a local industry,” he stated. He hailed generations of academics, administrators and staff, who have sustained ESUT through changing governments, difficult economic circumstances and the demands of educating successive generations. “In this regard, I want to assure the university community that the Enugu State Government is committed to the full implementation of the Academic Staff Union of Universities’ agreement with the Federal Government. “We are already speaking with legislators to firm up its inclusion in the budget for implementation as soon as possible,” he assured. Meanwhile, a major highpoint of the event was the conferment of an Honorary Doctorate Degree in Leadership, Governance, and Human Capital Development on Nwobodo. ESUT’s Vice Chancellor, Prof. Aloysius-Michaels Okolie, said it was in appreciation of the ex-governor’s huge contributions to the development of Enugu State, but also the entire old Anambra State, listing his many achievements. Another highpoint was the unveiling of Senator Nwobodo’s iconic status and the commissioning of a newly constructed road, Dr. Peter Mbah Drive, by the Governor. The post ESUT to be renamed after Jim Nwobodo – Mbah appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: MIIF exceeds 2026 target with GH¢9bn in mineral royalties two months ahead of schedule
items.description: The Minerals Income Investment Fund (MIIF) has exceeded its 2026 mineral royalty mobilisation target of GH¢6.9 billion, recording GH¢9 billion two months before the end of the year. Mrs Justina Nelson, MIIF’s Chief Executive Officer (CEO), announced this on Monday, November 16, during a breakout session on Mining, Minerals and Downstream Value Addition at the maiden Invest Ghana Summit in Accra. Addressing global investors, corporate leaders, policymakers and financial institutions at the summit, Mrs Nelson attributed the achievement to improvements in the Fund’s revenue mobilisation efforts. She noted that Ghana’s gold production rose 23.41 per cent in 2025, from 4.82 million ounces in 2024 to 5.94 million ounces. Small-scale mining accounted for 3.11 million ounces, representing 52.4 per cent of total production. She further disclosed that mineral royalty receipts rose from GH¢1.25 billion in 2020 to GH¢5.43 billion in 2025, a 334 per cent increase. The Fund also recorded a profit of GH¢1.1 billion in 2025. Mrs Nelson attributed the growth partly to increased gold production and the government’s introduction of the sliding-scale royalty regime. She noted that the Fund’s responsibilities extended beyond collecting mineral royalties to ensuring the revenues generated were prudently managed and invested to deliver sustainable returns for national development. She explained that MIIF was positioning its investment activities to support Ghana’s transition from exporting raw minerals to domestic processing, refining and manufacturing. Mrs Nelson called for stronger collaboration among the government, investors, mining companies, technology providers and development partners to unlock the full potential of Ghana’s mineral resources. She encouraged local and international investors to look beyond mineral extraction and explore opportunities across mining, processing, infrastructure and related industries. Ghana’s mineral wealth should ultimately be measured not only by production and exports but also by the industries developed, jobs created, technology acquired and opportunities generated for future generations. Meanwhile, Dr Cassiel Ato Baah Forson, the Minister of Finance, has announced the Government’s plans to invest US$1.5 billion in developing Ghana’s mineral processing industry to increase local value addition. Presenting the 2027 Budget Statement to Parliament on November 12, he said the investment would focus on manganese, bauxite, lithium and gold as part of efforts to create jobs, expand local industries and reduce the export of raw minerals. He also announced that by the end of 2026, at least 70 per cent of Ghana’s artisanal and small-scale gold would be refined locally, and the country’s total gold refining capacity was expected to reach 100 per cent by December 2028.

items.title: Farmer allegedly macheted over grazing dispute in Benue
items.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi A farmer, identified as Mr Terkura Orvanya, has reportedly been macheted by suspected herdsmen following a disagreement over the grazing of cattle on his cultivated farm at Ikpakena village, Makurdi Local Government Area of Benue State. Orvanya was said to have sustained serious machete wounds while attempting to defend himself against one of the herders after challenging them for allowing their cattle to destroy his melon farm. The incident was made public by Joseph Apahar, Media and Publicity Officer of IDP Benue State, in a social media post. According to Apahar, two herders were grazing their cattle on Orvanya’s melon farm when the farmer arrived and asked them to remove the animals from his cultivated crops. He alleged that the herders, despite being aware that the farm belonged to the farmer, showed no concern and refused to move the cattle away. Apahar said trouble started when Orvanya attempted to chase the animals out of his farm, prompting one of the herders to allegedly draw a cutlass and attack him. He said the farmer sustained machete wounds while attempting to shield himself from the attack, adding that Orvanya was receiving medical attention at a private hospital. Expressing concern over the incident, Apahar lamented what he described as the increasing cases of herders allowing their cattle to destroy cultivated crops, particularly farms containing crops ready for harvest or already harvested. He noted that such incidents were becoming increasingly common in the area, describing the development as a recurrence of the annual clashes between farmers and herders during harvest seasons after a period of relative peace. Apahar appealed to security agencies to urgently intervene to protect farmers and their investments from further destruction. “We are appealing to the security agencies to intervene urgently and help secure our crops before we are forced out of our villages, losing everything, and thereby reduced to nothing,” he said. He stressed that farmers should be allowed to harvest their crops without intimidation or attacks, insisting that their lives and livelihoods must be protected. “Our farmers deserve to harvest in peace. Our lives and livelihoods must be protected,” Apahar added. Efforts to reach the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Peter Aondongu, for comments on the incident were unsuccessful, as he could not be reached at the time of filing this report. items.title: FG targets raw mineral export ban, revenue tops N100bn
items.description: By Gabriel Ewepu The Federal Government is pushing to end the export of unprocessed solid minerals as part of efforts to deepen local value addition, boost industrialisation and create jobs, even as revenue from the sector crossed N100 billion in 2026. President Bola Tinubu stated this yesterday at the Nigeria Now! Investing in Energy, Infrastructure and Mining Summit in Abuja, themed, “United Nigeria, New Horizons, One Investment Destination.” Tinubu said Nigeria was determined to move beyond exporting raw mineral resources, stressing the need for investment in processing and beneficiation to strengthen domestic industries. “In mining, we’re equally determined to move beyond the export of unprocessed resources. Better geological information, transparent licensing, responsible exploration, and greater investment in beneficiation and processing must support Nigerian industries, skilled employment and meaningful benefits for host communities,” he said. The President said the government was working to build integrated value chains that would enable Nigerian enterprises to participate more actively in the mining industry and expand domestic capabilities. He urged investors to bring technology, finance and commercial expertise, assuring them of efforts to strengthen regulatory certainty and institutional support for sustainable returns. Earlier, Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dr Dele Alake, said reforms introduced by the Tinubu administration had increased revenue from the sector from N6 billion annually before the administration to N100 billion in 2026. “When I assumed office, the sector’s total annual revenue stood at just N6 billion. However, through reforms, the local value addition policy, the digitisation of mining processes, and efforts to sanitise operations within the sector, that figure increased from N6 billion to N38 billion by 2024. “By 2025, it had risen to N70 billion. And just about a week ago, the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) informed us that we had crossed the N100 billion mark this year,” Alake said. He attributed the growth to reforms and efforts to sanitise mining operations, including the establishment of Mining Marshals, which he said had apprehended over 300 illegal operators and recovered more than 100 mining sites. Meanwhile, Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Gboyega Oyetola, said revenue generated by agencies under his ministry rose from N700.79 billion in 2023 to N1.83 trillion in 2025. He cited improvements in maritime security, port reforms and approval of Nigeria’s first National Policy on Marine and Blue Economy, while urging investors to explore opportunities in shipping, ports, shipbuilding, fisheries, aquaculture and logistics. items.title: Alternative Dispute Resolution reduces court backlog by over 41,000 cases
items.description: Justice Gabriel Pwamang, Acting Chief Justice, said the Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) Programme has reduced traditional courts’ caseload by 41,431 cases since its introduction in 2005. He said last year, of the 6,836 cases referred to ADR, 2,722 were successfully settled, and it is currently connected to 138 courts across the country, with 336 trained mediators. Justice Pwamang announced this when he launched the 2026/2027 Legal Year ADR Week at the High Court in Tamale on Monday, saying ADR has become a significant tool for improving access to justice and easing pressure on the judicial system. ADR Week was instituted to raise awareness of the availability and benefits of ADR and encourage people with pending court cases to consider the mechanism. This year’s ADR Week is themed: “Strengthening the Foundations of Justice through Alternative Dispute Resolution and Technology”. Justice Pwamang said the figures showed that ADR was making a measurable contribution to reducing court workloads, saving judicial time and resources, and giving disputing parties opportunities to resolve their differences. “Each case successfully settled represents parties who have found a resolution without having to pursue a full trial. It also represents valuable judicial time and resources that can be devoted to disputes requiring adjudication”. He said cases resolved through ADR and entered as consent judgments were final and not subject to the appellate process, urging disputants and their lawyers to make ADR a preferred and trusted option for resolving conflicts. Justice Pwamang touched on technology, saying it offered significant opportunities to expand access to justice by enabling disputing parties to participate in mediation sessions without travelling long distances. Her Ladyship Justice Angelina Mensah-Homiah, Judge-in-Charge of the ADR Programme, said that, as part of ADR Week, the Judiciary would undertake a nationwide mass mediation exercise, identifying and referring cases for mediation. She encouraged Judges and Magistrates to refer appropriate cases to the ADR and urged the public to approach mediation with an open mind and a genuine willingness to reach mutually acceptable settlements. She also reminded mediators and ADR practitioners to comply with the requirements governing their practice. Mr Asuro Napari, Director, Legal Aid Commission, said the Commission received 261 cases in the first three quarters of the year, of which 170 were successfully resolved through ADR. He said the Commission remained committed to promoting ADR as an effective means of resolving disputes, especially for people who might otherwise struggle to access formal court processes. Mr Ali Adolf John, Northern Regional Minister, whose speech was read on his behalf, commended the Judiciary for promoting ADR, describing it as an important approach to improving access to justice and reducing the burden on the courts. Sheikh Arif Abdullah, Northern Regional Chairman of the Ghana Bar Association, urged lawyers to see mediation as an opportunity to secure practical solutions for their clients rather than merely a procedural requirement. Kampakuya-Naa Abukari II, Regent of Dagbon, who was represented at the launch, said traditional authorities have historically played important roles in resolving disputes through dialogue, consensus-building, and reconciliation. He said ADR complemented traditional conflict-resolution mechanisms and could help restore relationships and promote peaceful coexistence within communities.

items.title: Tinubu reiterates commitment to respecting court judgments
items.description: By Henry Ojelu President Bola Tinubu, yesterday, reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to respecting court judgments. He also conferred the Grand Commander of the Order of the Niger, GCON, Nigeria’s second-highest national honour, on renowned lawyer, Chief Wole Olanipekun, SAN. President Tinubu at the launch of a six-volume book, Wole Olanipekun Through the Cases, organised to celebrate the senior lawyer’s 75th birthday, 50 years at the Bar and 35 years as an SAN, said: “Our administration respects court judgments, even the ones we do not enjoy reading. We do not denigrate, attack or intimidate the judiciary. A government that bullies its judges only weakens its own foundation. “This administration passed the Judicial Officeholder Salary and Allowances Act 2024, reversing over 15 years of stagnation and delivering a 300 percent increase in the salaries of our Judicial Officers of the Superior Court of record. “We are not yet at our desired designation. But significant work is in progress, and the brighter future is now in closer view. We will be there, my Lordship. Our administration respects court judgment, even the one we do not enjoy reading. “We do not denigrate, attack or intimidate the judiciary,” President Tinubu reassured. Tinubu urged stakeholders in the justice sector to promote Nigeria as a business-friendly destination, stressing that timely judgments could strengthen investor confidence. “Every timely judgment is an advertisement for the Nigerian economy,” he said. He congratulated Olanipekun on his professional milestones, noting that the senior lawyer had positively impacted Nigeria and humanity through his legal practice and mentorship. Tinubu described Olanipekun as a phenomenal Nigerian and outstanding advocate who had upheld the traditions of excellence in the legal profession. The President also acknowledged the lawyer’s decades of loyalty and friendship, disclosing that Olanipekun had led his legal team for decades. “On a personal note, I celebrate decades of loyalty, friendship, commitment and reciprocity between Wole Olanipekun and I. He has led my legal team for decades. In politics, friends come and go. Wole came, and Wole stayed,” he said. Tinubu said Olanipekun also led the legal teams that defended three of his predecessors when their election victories were challenged. He said the senior lawyer had consequently served as lead counsel to four successive Nigerian presidents since 2007, describing the record as unprecedented. “Presidents change. Parties change. The Lead Counsel remains,” he said. President of the Senate Godswill Akpabio lauded President Tinubu for his commitment to justice, democracy, and national development. He assured the President that the National Assembly will continue to support all legal instruments that will promote justice, democracy and the rule of law. He also commended Chief Olanipekun for his contributions to the legal profession. Similarly, the Chief Justice of the Federation, Justice Kudirat Kere-Ekun, praised Wole Olanipekun for his immense contributions to the legal profession, believing that the publications being unveiled will further contribute to the intellectual depth, advocacy and enrichment of the nation’s jurisprudence. The Attorney-General of the Federation and Justice Minister, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, also spoke glowingly of Olanipekun and recalled several times they collaborated in court. As a lawyer, you don’t want to be on the opposite side of Chief Olanipekun, he said. Governor Biodun Oyebanji of Ekiti State eulogised Wole Olanipekun for enriching the legal profession, saying Ekiti State was proud of him. Minister of the FCT, Nyesom Wike, also gave a goodwill message. Chief Wole Olanipekun recalled his personal relationship with President Tinubu over the years and commended the President for his steadfastness, advocacy for democracy, and sacrifices. He revealed that at one such meeting, the President taught him the difference between legal and political jurisprudence. In his keynote address titled “The Rule of Law As a Catalyst for Private Sector Growth”, Tony Elumelu said the rule of law was vital to private sector growth and attraction of foreign investment, as entrepreneurs and investors were concerned about the right application of law as well as fair and speedy arbitration. According to him, trust is the currency that underpins economic activities and determines whether citizens cooperate with government, investors commit capital and businesses expand. Oyedele said: “Trust is the one currency that sits beneath all the other currencies. When trust is strong, citizens cooperate, capital flows, businesses invest, and reforms get a fair hearing. When trust is weak, even sound policies meet suspicion, and every explanation sounds like an excuse.” The minister said the economic consequences of negative narratives were often overlooked, adding that the country could lose investments and valuable human capital when its public image was dominated by stories of failure and hopelessness. He cited damaging perceptions expressed in phrases such as “Nigeria is finished,” “Nigeria is a scam,” and “Nigeria happened to me,” warning that such narratives could influence investment decisions and undermine confidence in the country’s economic prospects. Oyedele further explained that the cost was beyond reputational damage as, according to him, investors demand higher returns to compensate for perceived risks, postponement of expansion plans by businesses and seeking of opportunities elsewhere by talented Nigerians. He, however, acknowledged that citizens had the right to expose government failures, demand accountability and draw attention to the difficulties they faced. Responsible communication, he insisted, must not be confused with suppressing criticism, stressing that the country’s story must reflect both its challenges and progress. “Government and businesses cannot rely on publicity to conceal poor performance or substitute communication for service delivery. We cannot communicate our way out of conflicts,” he said. PR can’t cover bad leadership, global experts warn Meanwhile, global public relations experts have warned governments and corporate organisations to stop using PR, propaganda or strategic messaging to hide leadership failures. Trust, they said, could not be bought with publicity but earned through integrity, accountability and actions that match promises. The warning came at a session on Ethical Leadership and Trust in a Divided World at the ongoing 2026 World Public Relations Forum, WPRF, organised in Abuja by the Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication Management and the Nigeria Institute of Public Relations. The panel featured the Alliance’s regional council chairs for Europe, Asia-Pacific, Africa, Middle East and South Asia, and North America, and moderated by Chimdi Neliaku, Chair of the NIPR Young Professionals Hub. For Europe, Global Alliance Vice President and Chair of its European Regional Council, Silvia Arto, said ethical leadership was shown in personal conduct, not public declarations. To me, ethical leadership is lead by example. It’s walk the talk. It’s integrity,” she said, adding that integrity meant doing what was right, even when nobody was watching. From Asia-Pacific, the chair, Jaffri Osman, said effective leadership required more than intellectual intelligence, adding that motional and social intelligence matter just as much in building relationships across diverse communities. “Trust is built by leaders who understand beyond IQ. They have to understand EQ and SQ,” he said. Using Malaysia’s Sarawak region as an example of multicultural coexistence, Osman said professionals must understand local cultures, traditions and relationships to influence communities responsibly. For Africa, Chair Ms Irene Lungu Chipili identified political messaging, democratic competition and misinformation as major threats to public confidence. She questioned whether citizens could trust messages from political parties and governments, arguing that the credibility of the messenger was as important as the information. From the Middle East and South Asia, Chair Serra Gorpe said accountability, transparency and stakeholder engagement were essential to institutional legitimacy. “Legitimacy is accountability, transparency, stakeholder communication, engagement,” she said. Gorpe called for stronger ethics education in universities, urging institutions to use regional case studies rather than relying predominantly on Western textbooks. items.title: Burkina: compte rendu du Conseil des ministres du jeudi 19 novembre 2026
items.description: Le Conseil des ministres s’est tenu à Ouagadougou, le jeudi 19 novembre 2026, en séance ordinaire, de 09 H 00 min à 14 H 00 min, sous la présidence du Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORE, Président du Faso, Président du Conseil des ministres. Il a délibéré sur les dossiers inscrits à son ordre du jour, entendu des communications orales, procédé à des nominations, et autorisé des missions à l’étranger. I. DELIBERATIONS I.1. AU TITRE DE LA PRESIDENCE DU FASO Le Conseil a adopté deux (02) rapports. Le premier rapport est relatif à un projet de décret portant approbation des statuts particuliers de la Société d’Etat dénommée « Economat des Forces de défense et des Forces de sécurité », en abrégé « Economat-FDFS ». L’adoption de ce décret permet de doter la Société d’Etat Economat des Forces de défense et des Forces de sécurité de textes règlementaires en vue d’accomplir efficacement ses missions, conformément à la loi n°025/99/AN du 16 novembre 1999 portant règlementation générale des sociétés à capitaux publics. Le second rapport est relatif à l’inscription du « Projet RAAGA » sur la liste des projets spécifiques du Bureau national des Grands projets du Burkina (BN-GPB). Le « Projet RAAGA » porte sur la construction et l’aménagement de marchés modernes dans les arrondissements n°01 et n°04 de la ville de Ouagadougou et à Sarfalao à Bobo-Dioulasso. Il prévoit des complexes de marchés intégrés composés entre autres : – d’un bâtiment principal de type R+3 comprenant des étalages, un local sécurité, des sanitaires, des aires de restauration et diverses boutiques ; – des ouvrages annexes comprenant une infirmerie, une administration, un parking en silo pour permettre d’optimiser l’occupation des espaces ; – des bornes de recharges pour les véhicules électriques ; – des guichets automatiques de banque et de transfert d’argent. La mise en œuvre du « Projet RAAGA » permettra de renforcer la contribution du secteur commercial à la croissance économique nationale et de soutenir la dynamique de souveraineté économique et de développement endogène portée par la Révolution progressiste populaire. Le coût global de ce projet s’élève à 104 379 023 379 F CFA. Le financement est assuré par le budget de l’Etat. I.2. AU TITRE DU MINISTERE DE L’AGRICULTURE, DE L’EAU, DES RESSOURCES ANIMALES ET HALIEUTIQUES Le Conseil a adopté deux (02) décrets. Le premier décret porte modification des statuts particuliers du Fonds d’intervention pour l’environnement. Ce décret vise la modification du décret n°2015-901/PRES-TRANS/PM/ MEF/MERH du 27 juillet 2015 portant statuts particuliers du Fonds d’intervention pour l’environnement (FIE). Les innovations du décret sont entre autres : – la mise en conformité avec les nouveaux textes régissant les établissements publics et ceux définissant les attributions des départements ministériels ; – la redéfinition des missions du FIE pour consacrer son rôle d’instrument national de mobilisation, de gestion et d’allocation des ressources destinées à la protection de l’environnement, à la lutte contre les changements climatiques et à la promotion du développement durable ; – la diversification des modalités d’appui par l’introduction de nouveaux instruments financiers notamment les prêts concessionnaires et les prises de participation en complément des subventions. L’adoption de ce décret permet de doter le Fonds d’intervention pour l’environnement de nouveaux textes règlementaires en vue d’accomplir efficacement ses missions. Le second décret porte approbation des statuts particuliers révisés de FASO KOSAM. Ce décret est une relecture du décret n°2024-1766/PRES/PM/ MARAH/MICA/MEF du 31 décembre 2024 portant approbation des statuts particuliers de FASO KOSAM. Les principales innovations du décret sont : – la création d’un poste de Secrétaire général ; – la création de quatre (04) agences laitières dans les principaux bassins laitiers du pays. Il s’agit de l’Agence KOSAM du Centre, l’Agence KOSAM de l’Est, l’Agence KOSAM de l’Ouest et de l’Agence KOSAM du Nord ; – la reconfiguration du Conseil d’administration. L’adoption de ce décret permet de doter la société FASO KOSAM de nouveaux textes règlementaires en vue d’accomplir efficacement ses missions. I.3. AU TITRE DU MINISTERE DE L’ADMINISTRATION TERRITORIALE ET DE LA MOBILITE Le Conseil a adopté deux (02) décrets. Le premier décret porte nomination d’un Administrateur au Conseil d’orientation et de contrôle de l’Agence nationale de l’aviation civile (ANAC). L’adoption de ce décret permet la nomination du camarade Boulmonli Léonard LOMPO, Mle 104 413 C, Conseiller des affaires étrangères, Administrateur représentant l’Etat, au titre du ministère des Affaires étrangères au Conseil d’orientation et de contrôle de l’Agence nationale de l’aviation civile pour un premier mandat de trois (3) ans. Le second décret porte dissolution du Syndicat des pharmaciens du Burkina Faso (SPBF). Le coefficient appliqué au prix de cession des produits de spécialité est fixé au Burkina Faso à 1,32 depuis 1994. Entre février 2022 et janvier 2023, le Syndicat des pharmaciens du Burkina Faso a adressé plusieurs correspondances aux quatre grossistes-répartiteurs, en leur imposant de nouveaux coefficients nonobstant les textes en vigueur. Les sociétés Laborex Burkina, Tedis Pharma, Ubipharm ont donné suite à ces lettres en appliquant le coefficient de 1,48 sur les factures dès février 2023, à l’exception de la société Distribution pharmaceutique du Burkina Faso (DPBF). L’application de ce coefficient de 1,48 a entraîné une hausse des prix des médicaments de spécialité. A la suite de ces faits et après plusieurs enquêtes, la Commission nationale de la concurrence et de la consommation (CNCC) a saisi la Commission de l’UEMOA. Celle-ci par décision n°04/2026/COM/UEMOA du 27 février 2026, a établi que le SPBF et les trois grossistes-répartiteurs précités ont enfreint les dispositions du Traité de l’UEMOA. Elle a infligé une amende d’un million (1 000 000) F CFA au syndicat des pharmaciens et de cinquante millions (50 000 000) F CFA à chacun des trois grossistes-répartiteurs. La société DPBF a été mise hors de cause. Cette amende communautaire ne dispense pas l’Etat de tirer les conséquences des faits constatés à l’initiative d’une autorité burkinabè et supportées par les malades. Par conséquent, l’Etat a décidé de la dissolution du Syndicat des pharmaciens du Burkina Faso. L’adoption de ce décret permet la dissolution du Syndicat des pharmaciens du Burkina Faso, conformément à la loi n°011-2025/ALT du 17 juillet 2025 portant liberté d’association au Burkina Faso. I.4. AU TITRE DU MINISTERE DES AFFAIRES ETRANGERES Le Conseil a adopté un rapport relatif à une demande d’agrément pour la nomination d’un Ambassadeur Extraordinaire et Plénipotentiaire de la République du Rwanda auprès du Burkina Faso. Le Conseil a marqué son accord pour la nomination de Monsieur Moses RUGEMA, en qualité d’Ambassadeur Extraordinaire et Plénipotentiaire de la République du Rwanda auprès du Burkina Faso. I.5. AU TITRE DU MINISTERE DE LA JUSTICE Le Conseil a adopté deux (02) rapports. Le premier rapport est relatif aux projets spécifiques du ministère de la Justice. Ces projets spécifiques concernent la réalisation des études techniques, le suivi-contrôle et la construction du Palais de Justice de Bobo-Dioulasso (phase 1). Le coût global de ces projets spécifiques est de cinq milliards neuf cent cinquante-deux millions cent soixante-deux mille neuf cent soixante-cinq (5 952 162 965) F CFA TTC. Le financement est assuré par le budget de l’Etat. Le second rapport est relatif à un projet de décret portant nomination des membres de l’Autorité de régulation de la communication et du traitement des données à caractère personnel (ARCOD). L’adoption de ce décret permet la nomination de dix (10) membres à l’Autorité de régulation de la communication et du traitement des données à caractère personnel, conformément à la loi organique n°38-2026/ALP du 03 août 2026 portant dénomination, attributions, composition, organisation et fonctionnement de l’Autorité de régulation de la communication et du traitement des données à caractère personnel. I.6. AU TITRE DU MINISTERE DE LA SANTE Le Conseil a adopté quatre (04) rapports. Le premier rapport est relatif à un projet de décret portant approbation des statuts particuliers de l’Agence burkinabè de médecine traditionnelle et alternative (ABMTA). L’adoption de ce décret permet de doter l’Agence burkinabè de médecine traditionnelle et alternative de textes règlementaires en vue d’accomplir efficacement ses missions. Le deuxième rapport est relatif à un projet de décret portant approbation des statuts particuliers de « Faso Center for Disease Control and prevention », en abrégé « Faso CDC ». L’adoption de ce décret permet de doter Faso Center for Disease Control and prevention de textes règlementaires en vue d’accomplir efficacement ses missions. Le troisième rapport est relatif à des projets spécifiques du ministère de la Santé. Ces projets concernent la construction, l’équipement, le suivi architectural et le suivi-contrôle des travaux des Centres hospitaliers régionaux universitaires (CHRU) de Fada N’Gourma, Kaya, Koudougou et Banfora. Ils s’inscrivent dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre de la phase I (2026-2030) du Projet de construction et d’équipement de neuf (09) Centres hospitaliers régionaux universitaires (PCE/CHRU) d’une capacité de 500 lits chacun. Le coût de réalisation (construction et équipement) des quatre (04) CHRU s’élève à 324 000 000 000 F CFA hors taxe (HT). Le suivi architectural et le suivi-contrôle des travaux des quatre (04) CHRU se chiffrent à 2 400 000 000 F CFA TTC. Le financement est assuré par le budget de l’Etat. Le Conseil a instruit les ministres chargés du dossier de redimensionner le projet de construction du CHRU de Dédougou et d’y intégrer un Centre moderne de radiothérapie. Le quatrième rapport est relatif à des projets spécifiques du ministère de la Santé pour des activités critiques de préparation à la riposte contre d’éventuelles maladies infectieuses. Ces projets spécifiques visent à rendre opérationnels des centres de traitement des maladies infectieuses, aménager des sites de quarantaine pour les personnes contacts et constituer des stocks suffisants d’équipements et de protection des soignants. Le montant global de ces projets s’élève à un milliard cinq cent-vingt-un millions trente-neuf mille deux cent vingt-neuf (1 521 039 229) F CFA. Le financement est assuré par le budget de l’Etat. I.7. AU TITRE DU MINISTERE DE L’INDUSTRIE, DU COMMERCE ET DE L’ARTISANAT Le Conseil a adopté trois (03) décrets. Le premier décret porte approbation des statuts de la société d’économie mixte dénommée Société viticole du Burkina (SOVIB). L’adoption de ce décret permet de doter la Société viticole du Burkina de textes règlementaires en vue d’accomplir efficacement ses missions. Le deuxième décret porte approbation des statuts particuliers de l’Agence burkinabè de l’investissement et de promotion des exportations (ABIPEX). L’adoption de ce décret permet de doter l’Agence burkinabè de l’investissement et de promotion des exportations de textes réglementaires en vue d’accomplir efficacement ses missions. Le troisième décret porte création d’une société d’Etat dénommée Economat des Forces de défense et des Forces de sécurité (Economat-FDFS). L’Economat des Forces de défense et des Forces de sécurité a entre autres pour missions : – d’acquérir, de stocker et de gérer des denrées alimentaires et marchandises diverses ; – de mener des activités de transformation, de conditionnement, de traitement et de valorisation de produits agroalimentaires et industriels ; – de développer la production des filières locales (riziculture, élevage, pêche, agro-industrie) en lien avec ses besoins d’approvisionnement ; – de mener toute opération commerciale ou industrielle, mobilière, immobilière, financière, civile. Le capital social de l’Economat-FDFS est fixé à 1 000 000 000 F CFA. L’adoption de ce décret permet la création de la société d’Etat dénommée Economat des Forces de défense et des Forces de sécurité. I.8. AU TITRE DU MINISTERE DE L’ENERGIE, DES MINES ET DES CARRIERES Le Conseil a adopté un décret portant octroi d’un permis d’exploitation industrielle de grande mine de zinc à la Société de participation minière du Burkina Faso (SOPAMIB) PERKOA SA. La mine de zinc de Perkoa est située dans la commune de Réo, province du Sanguié, région de Nando. Cette mine avait fait l’objet d’un permis d’exploitation octroyé à la Société Nantou Mining Burkina Faso SA pour une durée de 20 ans. Elle a suspendu ses activités d’extraction industrielle à la suite de la tragédie survenue le 16 avril 2022. Cette suspension prolongée a entraîné des répercussions socio-économiques majeures notamment la perte d’emplois au niveau local, la perte de recettes fiscales et douanières pour l’Etat. La reprise des opérations par la SOPAMIB vise à sécuriser le patrimoine minier national, à relancer l’économie locale et à garantir une exploitation conforme aux exigences environnementales et de sécurité les plus strictes. La production totale attendue est estimée à 576 000 tonnes de concentré polymétallique pour une durée de vie de la mine estimée à 04 ans. Les investissements prévus s’élèvent à 37 milliards F CFA, pour un chiffre d’affaires prévisionnel de 270 milliards F CFA. La contribution directe du projet au budget de l’Etat s’élève à 84 827 405 843 F CFA. Il est attendu une contribution de 2 704 643 521 F CFA au Fonds minier de développement durant la vie du projet. La mise en œuvre du projet permettra la création et la consolidation de 400 emplois directs et environ 850 emplois indirects. L’adoption de ce décret permet l’octroi d’un permis d’exploitation industrielle de grande mine de zinc à la Société de participation minière du Burkina Faso (SOPAMIB) PERKOA SA. II. COMMUNICATIONS ORALES II.1. Le ministre de la Justice assurant l’intérim du ministre d’Etat, ministre de l’Administration territoriale et de la mobilité a fait au Conseil une communication relative à la célébration du 11 décembre 2026, placée sous le thème « Révolution progressiste populaire au Burkina Faso : une consécration des résistances à la domination coloniale et à l’impérialisme ». Cette manifestation vise à : – réaffirmer la souveraineté nationale ; – témoigner devant le peuple et la communauté internationale de la pleine maîtrise de notre destin national ; – valoriser les efforts de modernisation des équipements militaires et de transformation socio-économique ; – rendre un hommage solennel aux Forces armées nationales et de sécurité intérieure, ainsi qu’aux Volontaires pour la défense de la Patrie et au peuple résilient. La célébration du 11 décembre 2026 sera marquée par une grande parade militaire à Ouagadougou. Par ailleurs, le dispositif national d’organisation a été décliné au niveau régional avec la mise en place dans chaque région d’un comité régional d’organisation présidé par le gouverneur afin de favoriser une forte mobilisation des populations et renforcer les liens de cohésion et d’unité entre le peuple dans ses différentes composantes et son armée. II.2. Le ministre des Serviteurs du Peuple a fait au Conseil le compte rendu de la participation du Burkina Faso aux ateliers d’élaboration du guide commun pour l’harmonisation des pratiques en matière d’embauche des travailleurs migrants, du guide du travailleur migrant et de la convention sur la portabilité des prestations sociales des travailleurs dans l’Alliance des Etats du Sahel (AES). Ces ateliers se sont tenus respectivement du 17 au 21 septembre 2026 et du 17 au 24 septembre 2026 à Niamey, en République du Niger, conformément aux orientations définies dans la feuille de route de l’An II de la Confédération des Etats du Sahel. Cette feuille de route adoptée le 26 février 2026 à Ouagadougou, prévoit, au titre du volet Fonction publique, travail et protection sociale, l’optimisation de la gouvernance de la migration de la main-d’œuvre au sein de l’espace confédéral. La tenue de ces ateliers vise à mieux encadrer la mobilité des travailleurs des Etats membres, à faciliter les démarches administratives liées au recrutement des travailleurs migrants, à renforcer l’accès à l’information sur leurs droits et obligations et à garantir la continuité de leurs droits sociaux. La participation du Burkina Faso aux ateliers de Niamey s’inscrit dans la dynamique de consolidation de la coopération entre les Etats membres de la Confédération en matière de travail et de protection sociale. items.title: Cheddar brings Floyd Mayweather and Black Sherif together in Accra
items.description: Nana Kwame Bediako, popularly known as Cheddar, has brought boxing legend Floyd Mayweather Jr. and Ghanaian music star Black Sherif together during the American boxer’s visit to Ghana, highlighting the country’s growing influence in global entertainment and popular culture. The encounter in Accra offered Mayweather an opportunity to connect with one of Ghana’s most recognisable contemporary music talents, whose distinctive sound has earned him a growing international following. Cheddar, who welcomed the former world boxing champion to Ghana, has been accompanying him on engagements across the capital as part of efforts to showcase the country’s attractions and promote African tourism. The meeting with Black Sherif added a cultural dimension to the visit, connecting an international sporting icon with a Ghanaian artiste whose music has travelled well beyond the country’s borders. The encounter also underscored the potential of Ghana’s creative industry to support tourism promotion. Music, film and entertainment personalities can help generate international interest in the country, encouraging visitors to explore its culture, attend performances and experience its creative scene firsthand. For Cheddar, the meeting forms part of a broader effort to position Ghana as a destination that offers more than its historical attractions.

items.title: Dangote cement records 60% reduction in road traffic accidents
items.description: Dangote Cement Plc. has recorded a remarkable 60 per cent reduction in road traffic accidents, following the implementation of a comprehensive driver safety programme, underscoring the company’s unwavering commitment to protecting lives and promoting road safety across its transportation operations. The milestone was announced at the 2026 Customer Truck Scheme, CTS, Annual Driver Safety Award and Recognition Programme, where the company celebrated drivers who demonstrated exemplary safety performance and maintained accident-free records throughout the assessment period. The achievement builds on an earlier 30 percent reduction in road traffic accidents recorded in 2023, following the introduction of the company’s Safety Improvement Plan. As part of the initiative, approximately 3,000 drivers were trained in defensive driving techniques and safe road-use practices. According to the company, the sustained decline in accidents reflects the effectiveness of continuous driver training, behavioural monitoring, corrective interventions, and the deliberate recognition of safe driving practices. Speaking at the event on behalf of the Group Sales and Marketing Director, the National Sales Director of Dangote Cement Plc, Mr. Dolapo Ali, noted that the rapid expansion of the company’s transportation operations had made road safety a critical business priority. He disclosed that the CTS fleet had grown significantly from 469 trucks in 2017 to over 2,500 trucks today, increasing the need for a more structured and proactive safety management approach. “Our business has experienced tremendous growth over the years, and with that growth comes greater responsibility. As the number of trucks and drivers operating across our roads increases, so too does our exposure to road safety risks. Protecting lives and ensuring safe operations must therefore remain at the heart of our transport strategy,” he stated. Ali explained that road traffic accidents peaked in 2021 and 2022, prompting the company to introduce its Safety Improvement Plan in early 2023. A key component of the programme was an intensive defensive-driving training initiative through which approximately 3,000 drivers received professional safety training. The intervention delivered immediate results, with accident rates declining by 30 per cent in 2023 compared to the previous year, followed by a further 60 per cent reduction thereafter. To strengthen compliance and encourage safer driving behaviour, Dangote Cement also deployed advanced telematics technology across its fleet operations. The system enables real-time monitoring of critical driving behaviours, including overspeeding, harsh braking, and aggressive acceleration. items.title: Dollar scarcity, festive demand push Naira to N1,468/$
items.description: The naira yesterday continued its downward trend in both segments of the foreign exchange market, depreciating to N1,468 per dollar in the parallel market from N1,450 per dollar on Wednesday, as dwindling dollar supply and rising demand ahead of the festive season intensified pressure on the currency. Similarly, the naira weakened to N1,388 per dollar in the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market, NFEM, from N1,379.99 per dollar on Wednesday, representing a depreciation of N8.01. Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, showed that the indicative exchange rate in the official market rose to N1,388 per dollar. Consequently, the gap between the parallel and official markets widened to N80 per dollar from N70.01 per dollar on Wednesday. Meanwhile, interbank turnover in the NFEM rose by 59.13 per cent to $800.3 million from $502.9 million recorded on Wednesday. Vanguard analysis showed that the naira has depreciated by N95 in the parallel market since October 31, when it closed at N1,373 per dollar. Similarly, the currency has depreciated by N42 in the official market from N1,346 per dollar at the end of October. The nation’s external reserves also declined to $54.71 billion on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, according to CBN data, representing a decline of $554 million from the peak of $55.264 billion recorded on October 27, 2026. Commenting on the development, Chief Investment Officer of VNL Capital Asset Management, Dr. Ubah Jeremiah, said the naira’s weakness was driven more by tightening dollar supply and rising seasonal demand than by significant depletion of external reserves. He said foreign exchange inflows had fallen sharply to about $807.6 million in the latest week from $2.48 billion previously, reducing dollar availability in the market. “With fewer dollars coming in from autonomous sources, the market has leaned more heavily on CBN supply just as importers, businesses, and individuals step up purchases ahead of the festive season and year-end obligations,” he said. Ubah also blamed diverging monetary policy positions between the CBN and the US Federal Reserve for reinforcing pressure on the naira, noting that higher US yields and a stronger dollar could weaken the attractiveness of naira assets and encourage portfolio outflows. Meanwhile, parallel-market trader, Jubril Yinusa, attributed the depreciation to rising demand and limited dollar supply. “The naira has recorded continuous depreciation this week due to the high demand as the festive season approaches and low supply. Importation demand is also contributing to the depreciation of the naira,” he said. Another trader, Isa Dauda, said the festive season and the forthcoming election were also contributing to pressure on the currency. He said some foreign investors were adopting a wait-and-see attitude ahead of the elections, further limiting foreign exchange inflows. items.title: ‘He was a go-getter’ – Taiwo Obe, Providus Bank mourn Ajasa
items.description: THE Chairman and founder of Journalism Clinic, Mr Taiwo Obe, has described the late Online Editor of Vanguard Newspapers, Mr Femi Ajasa, as a go-getter, regretting that his death has robbed journalism of one of its brightest young professionals. Similarly, Providus Bank, one of Nigeria’s new-generation banks, has expressed sadness over Ajasa’s demise, saying his death is a loss not only to Vanguard but also to the media industry. In a condolence letter by its Group Head, Brand and Corporate Communication, Dafe Ivwurie, the bank said: “We were deeply saddened to learn of the death of Olufemi Ajasa. “By all accounts, he was an accomplished and highly respected digital journalist whose professionalism, dedication, and commitment to excellence contributed immensely to the growth and reputation of Vanguard’s digital media platforms. His passing at such a young age is a great loss not only to Vanguard but also to the Nigerian media industry.” Meanwhile, Obe, who took to his Facebook page to mourn Ajasa, described him as one of the first journalists trained at his clinic. He recounted the events that brought him close to the deceased and traced the history of their relationship until Ajasa’s death on Sunday. Obe said: “Circa 1997, TaijoWonukabe Limited, which I co-founded about two years earlier, moved from its garage office graciously donated to us by the prolific columnist, late Pini Jason Onyegbadue, into a three-bedroom bungalow on Bassie Ogamba Street, off Adeniran Ogunsanya, in Surulere, Lagos. “That property belonged to Madam Pemu, a relation of Sam Amuka-Pemu, the legendary journalist, Uncle Sam. “One day, not long after we moved in, Uncle Sam showed up, to greet Madam Pemu, who lived in a separate bungalow on the same premises. “I knew him then more by name than physical interactions. Either when he was leaving or as he alighted, I approached him, to introduce myself and after we exchanged pleasantries, he said: Money is good. See how you boys have changed this building. “From that day till date, we became connected. Fast forward to circa 2015: I had founded The Journalism Clinic and converted and renamed the hall which was the finishing room of PrintPro Projects Limited – the printing subsidiary of TaijoWonukabe – to The Hub – the training room of The Journalism Clinic at Anifowose, around the corner from Bassie Ogamba. “Uncle Sam visited one afternoon and declared ‘Vanguard will send people to all the training you will do here’.” He kept his word and the first paid training we had in The Hub included three participants from Vanguard Online Desk and Olufemi Ajasa was one of them. “A fine gentleman, two days ago, Vanguard reported his passing after a brief illness. Since that training, I had encountered Femi in various places and positions. He remained as respectful as ever; always go-getting and consistently impeccably-dressed. This really hit hard. Sùn re ò, Femooo,” he added. The post ‘He was a go-getter’ – Taiwo Obe, Providus Bank mourn Ajasa appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: L’attaque ukrainienne du pont de Crimée pourrait marquer un tournant
items.description: Dans la nuit du 16 au 17 novembre, l’armée ukrainienne a frappé avec une combinaison de missiles et de drones longue portée le pont de Crimée, qui relie la péninsule au kraï de Krasnodar, en Russie. L’opération était le fruit de plusieurs semaines de préparation, au cours desquelles l’armée ukrainienne a neutralisé les défenses aériennes russes situées autour du pont. Fabian Hoffmann, expert en missiles à l’Institut norvégien d’études de défense, à Oslo, considère que l’opération de frappe est probablement « l’une des plus complexes de l’histoire moderne » See How Ukraine Hit Putin’s Showpiece Bridge », The Wall Street Journal , 18 novembre 2026.'> 2 . Kiev a attaqué l'ouvrage à plusieurs reprises depuis le lancement de l'invasion à grande échelle, en ayant recours à des moyens différents comme un camion piégé (en 2022), des drones navals (en 2023) ou des explosifs sous-marins (en 2025). Il s’agit toutefois de la première fois que ces attaques conduisent à l’effondrement de l’une des deux arches du pont, celle de la section routière, un axe essentiel pour l’approvisionnement de la péninsule. Le 19 novembre, une nouvelle frappe, menée avec des missiles Neptune, a touché la section ferroviaire du pont et interrompu pendant plusieurs heures la circulation des trains. Cela fait plusieurs mois que Kiev mène une campagne de ciblage quasi systématique des routes et voies logistiques qui relient le territoire russe à la Crimée. L’armée ukrainienne revendique ouvertement depuis le mois de juin chercher à « couper la Crimée de la Russie » en ciblant les approvisionnements, mais des infrastructures stratégiques comme le pont de Crimée semblaient jusqu’à présent très difficiles à détruire ou à endommager sérieusement. Les conséquences de l’opération des 16 et 17 novembre pourraient être considérables. Avec une partie de la section routière du pont au fond du détroit de Kertch, l’armée russe ne dispose plus que d’une seule voie routière d’approvisionnement vers la péninsule : l’autoroute R-280, baptisée « Novorossiya » (« Nouvelle-Russie »). Or, comme le souligne l’analyste Clément Molin, cet axe est lui aussi fréquemment visé par des drones ukrainiens depuis plusieurs mois. Récemment, ces frappes ont touché Taganrog, en Russie, ainsi que les nombreux ponts sur le Mious entre Taganrog et Marioupol Publication de Clément Molin sur X , 18 novembre 2026.'> 3 . Faute d'alternative viable – la voie ferrée du pont, frappée à son tour le 19 novembre, reste exposée à de nouvelles frappes et les ferries encore en service ne peuvent pas se substituer aux camions qui assurent l'approvisionnement de la Crimée –, la péninsule pourrait connaître de graves pénuries. La gravité de la situation pour Moscou se reflète dans la réponse du Kremlin : depuis Shenzhen, Poutine a affirmé que la riposte russe serait « bien plus douloureuse que ce que le régime de Kiev a fait au pont », et a déclaré, à propos d’une trêve en mer ou de l’arrêt des frappes contre les infrastructures énergétiques : « Après les frappes contre le pont de Crimée, nous ne conclurons pas d’accord » Путин заявил, что ответ РФ на удары по Крымскому мосту будет более болезненным », Interfax , 19 novembre 2026.'> 4 . Hier, jeudi 19, les ambassades des Pays-Bas et d’Autriche à Kiev ont subi des dégâts lors d’une vague d’attaques russes. La Crimée, sous occupation russe depuis 2014 a une population de plus de deux millions de civils, ukrainiens et russes. Pour Kiev, la difficulté consiste à isoler la péninsule pour empêcher l’armée russe de se servir du territoire pour frapper le reste du pays et approvisionner le sud, sans nuire aux populations civiles. Réparer la structure du pont sera une opération complexe et coûteuse, que la Russie pourrait difficilement réaliser sans renforcer considérablement ses défenses ou obtenir de Kiev une forme de cessez-le-feu localisé – une option que Poutine semble exclure pour l’instant. L’article L’attaque ukrainienne du pont de Crimée pourrait marquer un tournant est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: Slain anchorperson’s husband released on bail in Rawalpindi
items.description: ISLAMABAD: A local court on Thursday granted post-arrest bail to the husband of anchorperson Rabia Ahsan against surety bonds of Rs200,000 after the deceased’s family informed the court that the fatal shooting was accidental and they did not wish to pursue the case. An additional district and sessions judge Rawalpindi allowed the bail application after the deceased anchorperson’s mother, brother and sister appeared before the court and submitted affidavits stating that Rabia Ahsan had died as a result of an accidental shooting and that they had no objection to the release of the accused. Rabia Ahsan died of a gunshot wound at her residence in Gulshanabad on Nov 8. Following the incident, police registered a murder and illegal arms case against her husband on a complaint lodged by her brother and subsequently arrested him. During the subsequent proceedings, however, the deceased’s family maintained that the shooting was accidental and submitted affidavits to this effect before the court. After recording the family members’ statements and examining the affidavits, the court approved the accused’s post-arrest bail against surety bonds of Rs200,000. Published in Dawn, November 20th, 2026

items.title: Pakistan 'unequivocally' condemns Houthi attack on Riyadh’s tallest skyscraper
items.description: Pakistan on Friday “unequivocally” condemned a Houthi attack on Riyadh’s tallest skyscraper, which serves as the headquarters of Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund. “This act of aggression constitutes a grave violation of the sovereignty of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia,” the Foreign Office (FO) said in a statement condemning Thursday’s attack, without naming the tower. Saudi state-run news agency SPA reported, citing the kingdom’s civil defence, that the attack caused material damage to several floors of the building and nearby buildings, but no injuries were reported. The statement carried by the SPA did not identify the tower, but an accompanying photograph published by the agency showed the Public Investment Fund Tower. The strike blew out windows across seven to eight floors of PIF Tower, bending parts of its metal facade. It was the second time in less than two weeks that a Houthi attack damaged a landmark in Riyadh’s financial district, with state oil company Aramco’s building hit in a Nov 8 attack. The Houthis have been firing at Saudi airports and oil infrastructure since Yemen’s frozen civil war reignited in July amid the US-Iran conflict. The renewed fighting has shattered a UN-brokered truce reached in 2022 that largely halted cross-border attacks between the Saudi-led coalition, which backs Yemen’s internationally recognised government, and the Houthis, who control the capital, Sanaa. Pakistan, which is party to two defence agreements along with Saudi Arabia — the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement and the Saudi Mutual Defence Agreement that empower the parties to treat an attack on any one of them as an attack on all — has expressed its solidarity with the kingdom amid the escalation. In its statement on Friday regarding Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, the FO said: “The continued targeting of civilian infrastructure and economic facilities endangers innocent lives and poses a serious threat to regional peace and security. Such reprehensible attacks must cease forthwith.” It added that Pakistan stood firmly with the government and people of Saudi Arabia. “It supports the kingdom’s legitimate right to defend its sovereignty and territorial integrity and to safeguard its citizens and residents. Pakistan has been and will continue to make all efforts for achieving lasting peace and stability in the region,” the statement said.

items.title: Tinubu moves to achieve 40% fares reduction under NACTP
items.description: President Bola Tinubu in his determination to achieve the 40 percent fare-reduction target under the National Affordable CNG Transit Programme NACTP, as outlined in his renewed hope agenda 2.0, has welcomed plans by Yutong, the world’s largest bus manufacturer and a global leader in electric and CNG-powered buses, to establish a CNG bus assembly plant in Nigeria. This followed his invitation to the Chinese automotive giant to support the expansion of affordable mass transportation across the country. Special Adviser to the President on Information and Strategy, Mr. Bayo Onanuga, in a statement, yesterday, noted that the investment would support the National Affordable CNG Transit Programme, NACTP, in collaboration with state governments, which targets transport fare reductions of approximately 40 percent on participating routes, in line with the President’s renewed hope agenda 2.0 for 2027–2031. Under the agreement with the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles, Pi-CNG & EV, Yutong will supply an initial 300 CNG-powered buses, with the first 100 expected to arrive in Lagos by the end of December 2026. Subsequent buses will be assembled in Nigeria through YP Automobiles Bus Assembly at the former Leyland Automotive plant in Ibadan, Oyo State, reviving local industrial capacity, reducing dependence on imported vehicles and creating employment opportunities for Nigerian engineers, technicians and other workers. Yutong, which sold 49,518 buses globally in 2025, brings extensive experience in mass transit manufacturing, with operations across international markets and a track record of supporting local assembly and public transportation projects in several countries. The President noted that the investment comes as CNG adoption continues to increase nationwide, supported by the expansion of refuelling infrastructure through Pi-CNG & EV, the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund, MDGIF, and private sector investors. These interventions include deploying Mobile Refuelling Units (MRUs) and the President’s directive for 2,000 additional CNG refuelling infrastructure units nationwide, laying the foundation for a wider rollout of affordable commercial buses. President Tinubu emphasises that reducing the daily cost of transportation for Nigerians remains the central objective of these investments. The President notes that millions of Nigerians depend on commercial transportation to get to work, take their children to school, travel to markets and move goods between communities. For many households, transportation consumes a significant portion of their daily earnings. He stresses that the lower operating costs of CNG-powered vehicles must translate into lower fares for passengers, allowing workers, traders and families to retain more of their income for food, education and other essential needs. The President points to the approximately 40 percent fare-reduction target under the NACTP, as outlined in his renewed hope agenda 2.0, and reiterates his administration’s determination to work with state governments and transport operators to extend affordable CNG transportation to more routes nationwide. He welcomed Yutong’s decision to establish local assembly capacity in Nigeria, noting that the investment would help sustain the supply of affordable commercial buses while facilitating technology transfer, creating skilled employment and strengthening the country’s automotive industry. The post Tinubu moves to achieve 40% fares reduction under NACTP appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 16e édition de la Biennale de l’Art africain contemporain de Dakar: Sacre du Congolais Beau Disundi
items.description: L’artiste visuel congolais Beau Disundi a reçu le Grand Prix du chef de l’Etat « Léopold Sédar Senghor ». 16e édition de la Biennale de l’Art africain contemporain de Dakar. Le Jury international de la Biennale de Dakar 2026 a consacré Beau Disundi du Grand Prix du Chef de l’Etat « Léopold Sédar Senghor ». La distinction majeure de la Biennale de l’Art contemporain de Dakar, dotée d’un trophée et de 20 millions de FCfa, est remportée par l’artiste visuel congolais dont le travail examine les intersections entre histoire, économie, circulation des biens et effets culturels de la mondialisation. Il s’intéresse notamment à la morue comme objet symbolique des échanges commerciaux, des héritages coloniaux et des processus d’acculturation. L’Ethiopienne Miriam Hillawi Abraham a obtenu le Prix de la Révélation « Ministère de la Culture, de l’Artisanat et du Tourisme », avec 10 millions de FCfa. Miriam Hillawi Abraham est une designer pluridisciplinaire originaire d’Addis-Abeba, en Éthiopie. Forte d’une formation en architecture, elle axe son travail sur la préservation expérimentale et la perpétuation du patrimoine matériel et des savoirs immatériels du continent africain. Sa méthodologie l’amène à endosser le rôle de tisserande, entrelaçant des fils qui relient entre eux des mondes dispersés. Lire aussi: Biennale de Dakar : l’Afrique transforme ses fragilités en force créatrice Le Prix UEMAO, d’un chèque de 8 millions de FCfa, est revenu à l’artiste de la Guinée Bissau, Nú Barreto. Formé à la photographie puis diplômé de l’École nationale des métiers de l’image des Gobelins, il développe une pratique pluridisciplinaire et politiquement engagée qui traverse dessin, peinture, collage, photographie, vidéo et installation. Son langage visuel, souvent construit autour du noir, du rouge, de silhouettes humaines et de signes graphiques, aborde violences sociales, inégalités, mémoire collective et responsabilités politiques. Le Prix de la CEDEAO de l’Intégration, remis par le Commissaire de l’institution régionale, le Professeur Nassirou Bako-Arifari, a récompensé le duo Vanessa Amoah Opoku & Joy Weinberger (Ghana / Allemagne). Les deux reçoivent en prime 5 millions de FCfa. Elles développent ensemble une pratique collaborative à la croisée de l’image numérique, de l’installation et du textile. Le duo part de l’histoire familiale ghanéenne d’Opoku et combine scans 3D en nuages de points, archives sonores, photographies familiales, structures sculpturales et tissages Le Prix du Maire de la Ville de Dakar, en plus de 5 millions de FCfa, est attribué, à titre posthume, au défunt artiste Papisto Boy. De son vrai nom Pape Mamadou Samb, né en 1951 et décédé en 2014, il incarne la résilience et l’abnégation mises au service d’un projet artistique. Autodidacte, Papisto Boy développe sur les murs de Dakar une écriture picturale singulière qui allie à la fois une démarche mémorielle et une chronique contemporaine qui magnifie les « missionnaires » importants de notre époque (saints, musiciens, politiques, intellectuels ou encore personnages légendaires). Le Jury international de la Biennale de Dakar 2026 est composé de sa présidente, la photographe éthiopienne Aïda Muluneh, ainsi que de l‘artiste visuelle cubaine Maria Magdalena Campos-Pons, de l’artiste visuelle protéiforme tunisienne Mouna Jemal Siala (Prix du Ministre de la Culture de la Biennale de Dakar 2010), l’artiste ghanéen Ibrahim Mahama et grande figure de la création contemporaine, et enfin le plasticien sénégalais de la deuxième génération de l’Ecole de Dakar, Abdoulaye Ndoye. Mamadou Oumar KAMARA

items.title: Pakistan, 14 other nations welcome UK, Australia sanctions on Israeli settlements
items.description: Pakistan, along with 14 other countries, has welcomed the imposition of sanctions by the United Kingdom and Australia in response to Israeli settlement activities in the occupied Palestinian territory and expressed hope that the decisions would encourage others to follow suit. Britain said on Tuesday it would impose sanctions on eight Israeli construction companies involved in building settlements in ‌the occupied West Bank, as part of its effort to protect the idea of a two-state solution. Australia followed by imposing sanctions on three Israeli individuals and four organisations for illegal settlement expansion and ​settler violence in the West Bank on Wednesday, saying those actions were extinguishing the possibility of ‌a two-state solution. In a joint statement on Thursday, the foreign ministers of Pakistan, Jordan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Somalia, Indonesia, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, Turkiye, Kuwait, Algeria, Niger, Palestine, Libya, and Maldives welcomed the decisions. They also welcomed the United Kingdom’s decision to sanction an organisation obstructing the delivery of humanitarian aid to Gaza, the statement said. “The ministers also expressed support for all efforts to ensure accountability, including through appropriate international measures and the imposition of sanctions on entities and individuals responsible for settlement activities, including the E1 settlement plan, as well as those that support, facilitate or implement settlement expansion and annexation policies,” it added. The E1 settlement project would bisect the Israeli-occupied West Bank and cut it off ​from East Jerusalem, fragmenting the land Palestinians hope will form the heart of a state. In the joint statement, the ministers renewed their “strongest condemnation of Israel’s continued settlement policies in the occupied Palestinian territory, particularly the ‘E1’ settlement plan and related settlement activities east of occupied East Jerusalem”. The statement said the ministers considered the measures by the UK and Australia to be in line with international law and relevant United Nations resolutions, including the “obligation of all states not to recognise as legal the situation arising from Israel’s unlawful occupation and not to render aid or assistance in maintaining the situation created by Israel’s occupation”. In this regard, they reiterated their call for Israel to rescind all measures taken in connection with settlement activities and other measures aimed at altering the geographic and demographic character of the occupied Palestinian territory. Moreover, they condemned the “Israeli military escalation in Gaza” and called for “the full and immediate implementation of President Trump’s Comprehensive Plan to End the Gaza Conflict, to ensure security and stability, address the humanitarian situation, facilitate reconstruction and recovery, and lay the foundations for lasting peace”. The ministers underscored that Gaza was an integral part of the occupied Palestinian territory and that the only viable path to achieving a just, lasting, and comprehensive peace in the territory was the “implementation of the two-state solution, through the realisation of an independent, sovereign, contiguous, and viable Palestinian State, based on the Jun 4, 1967 lines, with East Jerusalem as its capital, in accordance with international law and the relevant United Nations resolutions”. Sanctions The UK’s measures on Tuesday targeted eight companies, including Har Hevron Development Company Ltd, Hemdat Shomron Ltd and SAG (Velvel) Construction and Development Ltd, for asset freezes and director disqualifications. The UK government announced the sanctions package shortly before ​the final deadlines for the E1 tender. On Wednesday, Australia also imposed sanctions in response to settlement activities in the West Bank, with Foreign Minister Penny Wong saying in a statement: “The sanctioned individuals and organisations have actively participated in the planning, coordination and establishment of ​new settlements, including raising funds, recruitment of volunteers and providing support to violent settlers.” Daniella Weiss, leader of the settler ⁠organisation Nachala and an advocate for the expulsion of Palestinians from Gaza, is among those sanctioned. ​Another sanctioned individual, Eliav Libi, has accelerated the expansion of settlements in the West Bank through his construction ​company. The measures prohibit Australians and Australian businesses from trading with, or providing support to, the sanctioned individuals and organisations. Wong also said that violence at the E1 settlement project in recent weeks had undermined the prospect of a two-state solution. She said she had also spoken to Israeli Foreign ​Minister Gideon Saar about Australia’s latest round of sanctions. “I outlined our position … I ​said we ⁠do not agree with, we oppose the settlement activities. We have had a long-standing position on this,” Wong told ABC Radio .
