items.title: The Limits of Positive Thinking
items.description: A s anxious Americans dealt with a cascade of computer failures over the past week, Donald Trump offered this advice: “Relax.” The air-traffic-control system, email providers, banks, airlines, and even the internal communications system of the country’s biggest intelligence agency had all seen outages, fueling fears of digital conspiracy. But they weren’t connected, the president assured Fox News. And hackers were not behind the outages, he insisted, because no one would dare risk retaliation by the United States. Companies were simply replacing outdated equipment, “and things happen when you put in new equipment,” he said. There was nothing to see here, no cause for alarm. “Everything’s good.” Digital-security experts are not nearly so sanguine. They see something new and potentially ominous that’s fueling these hugely disruptive outages: artificial intelligence. Companies haven’t been replacing old equipment so much as rapidly patching newly discovered flaws in their systems with the help of sophisticated AI that can quickly spot vulnerabilities. And why are companies moving so fast? Because attackers have AI too. The FBI warned this week about an AI-enabled tool set, called ARTEX, that “cybercriminals and state-aligned hackers” are using to identify weakness and develop attacks in under three hours. None of the affected companies has said that it thinks its systems went down because of an attack. But security experts told us that in the past few weeks, they have been struggling to keep up with an onslaught of attempted hacks from AI-enabled adversaries. And rushing to harden lots of computer infrastructure all at once can be messy and inconsistent, explaining some of the disruptions. Trump has never fully reckoned with the risks of AI. He prefers to call it “superintelligence,” an odd choice given that that’s the term some doomsayers use for AI that becomes self-aware and tries to wipe out humanity. The president frames the race to develop advanced AI as an existential contest between China and the United States. “Whoever wins AI wins,” he is fond of saying. The Defense Department has deployed AI systems across its networks with seemingly little regard for the risks of using them in combat. Trump has avoided creating safety regulations and guardrails and has followed the counsel of executives whose fortunes depend on AI expansion. That includes ex–Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who has consistently downplayed the risk of out-of-control AI, calling apocalyptic scenarios “made-up” or baseless. When it comes to developing and deploying the technology, Trump is all gas and no brakes. For a different president, the nerve-racking outages of the past week might have been a moment for sober reflection on whether the United States is prepared for what’s coming. Even some Republicans are asking for that, as are some Democrats. “It feels like every day brings another reminder that AI is moving faster than our ability to manage its consequences,” Senator Mark Warner of Virginia, a Democrat who is in line to chair the Senate Intelligence Committee in the next Congress, said in a statement. Warner has proposed legislation that would subject AI models to greater scrutiny and safety checks. “Americans deserve clear, reliable information and a government that is prepared to respond,” Warner said. But the administration seems not to grasp how worried many Americans are at suddenly being unable to check their bank balance or read their email. The disappearance of everyday conveniences comes after months of dark warnings about rogue AI agents and renewed fears of cyberattacks from Iran. The French government publicly accused Iran last week of remotely sabotaging food-refrigeration units and causing mass spoilage in grocery stores. Trump may insist that there’s nothing to be concerned about, but even some of his allies fear that something bigger is at play. “If this is all a coincidence,” Senator Josh Hawley of Missouri, a Republican, told reporters on Tuesday, “it’s like the greatest coincidence in the history of the world.” N ormally, in the middle of a domestic crisis, an administration tries to speak with one voice and tell a coherent story to an anxious public. But as bank websites crashed at the same time as stranded passengers slept in airports, no one in the administration seemed to know what was happening or who was in charge of fixing things. On Monday, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, who is supposed to lead the government’s response to domestic cybersecurity incidents, suggested that artificial intelligence deployed on computer networks was “self-fixing itself.” In the scenario he described, recent network collapses were the result of a big, messy patching job. That is close to what experts think is continuing to happen. But Mullin attributed his understanding to a tech leader, whom he declined to name, telling Fox News that his theory “kind of makes sense.” This uncertain description, from an official with access to an array of classified government intelligence and seasoned briefers, did little to allay concerns. [ Read: The secretary of imprecision ] The unit within Mullin’s department that should be running point in this crisis, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency , has lost almost a third of its 3,200 employees since Trump returned to office two years ago. The White House wants to cut the budget for some agency programs, including election security, by $700 million next year. When we went to the CISA website today, we found guidance about recent incidents, forms for reporting cyberattacks, and a two-month-old handbook for “Communicating Under Pressure.” “During service outages, clear communication matters,” CISA unironically advised. Officials dismissed any connection between the computer failures and the deep staffing and budget cuts at the agency. “The implication that the recent events would not have occurred if CISA had more employees is patently false,” a White House official said. The new director of national intelligence, Jay Clayton, told a congressional committee yesterday that “the timing of these ​incidents can raise questions, ​and it should,” but he insisted that the outages were coincidental and “associated with maintenance and ​technical ​changes.” Clayton also blamed the patching of vulnerabilities, but he didn’t blame AI. Marco Rubio , the secretary of state and the national security adviser, appeared initially confused when a reporter asked at a press conference in Manila whether AI had played a role in the outages. He said he couldn’t confirm that that was the case but explained why AI hypothetically could have led to the systems failing. Rubio stressed that “people are fearful; people are uncertain” and said that it was important for the administration to “share with them transparently what we know.” T rump’s habit, when he is confronted with a crisis, is to rely on the power of positive thinking. In the first weeks of 2020, he was slow to sound the alarm on a new virus discovered in China, reportedly for fear of rattling financial markets and upsetting Xi Jinping. By the time he left office a year later, some 400,000 people in the United States had died of COVID-19 . A similar dynamic now seems to be at work. Trump has resisted calls even from within the AI industry to regulate the technology, fearing that government interference will stymie innovation and slow growth. The president knows that AI companies are propping up the stock market and that U.S. economic expansion depends largely on the construction of new data centers, which are essential for developing more powerful AI models. Trump was in China this week for meetings with Xi and Vladimir Putin, and he indicated to allies that he didn’t want anything to distract from those sessions. That could explain the at-times-nonexistent messaging from the White House. During the height of Friday’s ground stop by the Federal Aviation Administration—which does not appear to have been caused by AI-related patching—Trump was huddled in the Oval Office with the actor Jon Voight, talking about Hollywood tax rebates. He stayed out of sight for days, leaving Mullin and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy to make a widely panned series of appearances in which they largely blamed the Biden administration and demanded money from Congress. One air traffic controller told us that everything he and his colleagues had learned about the nationwide ground stop—an event that has happened only three times this century—came from the same general announcement Duffy had made to the public. The controller said that he had received no information internally about the outage and its causes. Officials privately acknowledge that an extraordinary amount of work needs to be done to fend off the relentless and increasing AI attacks. But the president’s advisers may be wary of telling the public the truth about the scale of the threat because they don’t want to make Trump angry, two Republicans close to the White House told us on the condition of anonymity to discuss private conversations. [ Read: Trump sets the olive branch on fire ] In his Fox News interview, Trump said that journalists were exploiting the computer crashes for political purposes: “The press is sort of having a lot of fun with it. If these things would’ve happened two years ago, three years ago, in the Biden administration, which was grossly incompetent and corrupt, nobody would’ve mentioned it.” Journalists extensively covered similar breakdowns, including a nationwide ground stop in 2023 and the discovery of a massive penetration of U.S. telecom networks by China, through an actor known as Salt Typhoon, the following year. Trump insisted on Fox News that the weeklong parade of cyber horribles was a mere coincidence. “I’ll let you know if there’s a problem,” he said. After the past week, the bar for what Trump considers to be a problem is looking awfully high. Isaac Stanley-Becker and Madison Hahamy contributed to this article.

items.title: El minuto de oro de Alberto Núñez Feijóo
Dos hombres y un elefante en la habitación
items.description: La democracia necesita de un debate televisado protagonizado por quienes aspiran a gobernar un país. Un debate como el que tuvo lugar ayer permite romper con las estrategias de segmentación y de fragmentación de mensajes que dominan ahora las estrategias de campaña. Los debates se convierten así en el único formato en el que los candidatos se encuentren solos, frente a frente, pero observados por todos, especialmente por los verificadores. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Bobo-Dioulasso : Un greffier écroué pour une affaire d’escroquerie de 4,5 millions FCFA autour d’une fausse vente aux enchères
items.description: Un greffier en service au Tribunal du travail de Bobo-Dioulasso est poursuivi pour des faits présumés d’escroquerie et d’abus de fonction. Il lui est reproché d’avoir encaissé 4,5 millions de FCFA auprès d’un particulier en lui promettant trois véhicules dans le cadre d’une prétendue vente aux enchères de la Cour d’appel. Une affaire présumée d’escroquerie impliquant un auxiliaire de justice est entre les mains du parquet de Bobo-Dioulasso. Un greffier en fonction au Tribunal du travail de la ville est poursuivi pour avoir prétendument organisé une fausse opération de vente aux enchères de véhicules, qui lui aurait permis d’obtenir 4,5 millions de FCFA auprès d’un particulier. Selon un communiqué du Procureur du Faso près le Tribunal de grande instance (TGI) de Bobo-Dioulasso, les faits remontent à mai 2026. Le mis en cause aurait proposé à un particulier d’acquérir trois véhicules présentés comme faisant partie d’une vente aux enchères qui devait être organisée par la Cour d’appel de Bobo-Dioulasso. Convaincu de la réalité de l’opération, le particulier aurait remis au greffier la somme de 4,5 millions de FCFA en vue de concrétiser cette acquisition. Mais la vente annoncée n’a finalement jamais eu lieu. Le plaignant aurait alors découvert que l’opération était fictive et qu’elle aurait été montée dans le but de lui soutirer de l’argent. Le greffier placé sous mandat de dépôt À la suite de la plainte, le parquet a diligenté une enquête pour faire la lumière sur cette affaire. Au terme des investigations, le greffier a été poursuivi pour des faits présumés d’escroquerie et d’abus de fonction, sur la base des articles 332-12, 613-1 et 613-2 du Code pénal. Il a ensuite été placé sous mandat de dépôt, dans l’attente de la suite de la procédure judiciaire. Le parquet appelle les éventuelles victimes à se manifester Dans son communiqué daté du 18 novembre 2026, le Procureur du Faso, Sékou Traoré, réaffirme la détermination du parquet à lutter contre toutes les formes de délinquance et à veiller au respect de la loi. Il invite par ailleurs toute personne disposant d’informations sur de telles pratiques, ou estimant avoir été victime de faits similaires, à saisir son parquet afin de contribuer à la manifestation de la vérité. L’article Bobo-Dioulasso : Un greffier écroué pour une affaire d'escroquerie de 4,5 millions FCFA autour d’une fausse vente aux enchères est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Feijóo sorprende ante un Sánchez incómodo
items.description: La rivalidad entre Pedro Sánchez y Alberto Núñez Feijóo tiene mucho de personal, lamentablemente. Sus intercambios en las sesiones de control parlamentarias han dejado un terreno de humillaciones y descalificaciones difíciles de superar. No tienen comunicación personal directa como debería ser recomendable entre un presidente y un líder de la oposición. El desprecio mutuo supura en sus miradas y se refleja en toda su comunicación: desde lo que dicen a cómo lo dicen. Y sus cuerpos hablan. No se soportan y, con ello, renuncian a convencer y a entender lo que representa el adversario. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Jéssica Feijóo vs. Maricarmen Sánchez
items.description: Una y otra vez esperamos los debates con la excitación de una ronda de penaltis, y una y otra vez los debates se encargan de aplicar hielo sobre nuestra calentura: nadie deja nunca al rival a cero, nadie da nunca un golpe triunfal, nadie se ha retirado nunca mostrando al público la simbólica cabellera del contrario. Para desatar de verdad el fervor hay que conocer el resultado final, y para conocer el resultado final hay que esperar hasta el domingo. Para más frustración, ni siquiera este domingo. Y, con el precedente de 2023 — Feijóo ganó el debate y Sánchez la presidencia —, ya sabíamos que en diez días no hay sensación de derrota o de triunfo que no pueda aguarse. Para más inri, de este cara a cara de 2026 podemos pensar que el marcador provisional, ya que no el resultado final, indica tablas. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Feijóo se lanza al ataque ante un Sánchez que evita el cuerpo a cuerpo
items.description: Alberto Núñez Feijóo fue en tromba contra Pedro Sánchez, no solo con una enmienda a la totalidad de sus ocho años de gestión, sino cuestionando una y otra vez tanto la competencia como la integridad y decencia del presidente. Ante las descargas de Feijóo, siempre en tono acusatorio, el candidato socialista evitó el choque, adoptando una actitud por momentos autocrítica, respondiendo a los duros golpes de su adversario con cierta mesura. Es la síntesis del primer —y único— cara a cara entre los dos principales aspirantes a la presidencia, que tuvo lugar este jueves. Aunque primero en las encuestas y favorito para llegar a La Moncloa, Feijóo renunció al papel de solemnidad presidencial y se lanzó a degüello contra Sánchez, que, aunque necesitado de remontada, optó por minimizar el cuerpo a cuerpo y centrarse en la defensa de su gestión. A diferencia del debate de 2023 , no se exasperó ante su adversario. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Maquillaje de tanatorio y poca moderación: aciertos y errores televisivos del debate de Sánchez y Feijóo
items.description: Los debates electorales organizados por la Academia de la Televisión son uno de esos pocos eventos —más allá del discurso navideño del Rey— en los que da igual qué número del mando a distancia se pulse, que se va a encontrar la misma imagen. Solo había escapatoria si se conectaba con alternativas más punkis como Boing, Neox o DKiss. El cara a cara de este jueves entre los dos principales candidatos a la presidencia del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez y Alberto Núñez Feijóo, es uno de los momentos culmen de la campaña hacia el 29-N. Los debates electorales casi se pueden entender como un subgénero televisivo, uno que nació para que los espectadores pudieran tener un conocimiento más directo de los programas electorales y conocer mejor a los candidatos, pero que se han ido transformando en acontecimientos mediáticos, eventos televisivos más allá de la pura política. Esta es la sociedad del espectáculo, así que juguemos con sus reglas. Seguir leyendo

The $1.3 billion Chinese-built megaport in Chancay, just north of the capital Lima, marks its second year of operations with plans to become the most important port hub on Latin America’s Pacific coast. items.title: La Cour d’appel de Tunis rend son verdict dans l’affaire Lourimi & Gharbi
items.description: La chambre criminelle spécialisée dans les affaires de terrorisme près la Cour d'appel de Tunis a rendu son verdict dans l'affaire visant Ajmi Lourimi et Mossaâb Gharbi. La justice a décidé de confirmer le verdict rendu le 3 juillet 2026 en première instance condamnant le secrétaire général d'Ennahdha Ajmi Lourimi et le militant du même parti, Mossaâb Gharbi, à trois ans de prisonn affirme Mosaïque FM, ce jeudi 19 novembre 2026, en citant une source proche du dossier. Cette affaire remonte à l'année 2024, lorsque les agents de la brigade de recherches et d'investigations de la Garde nationale de Tebourba ont procédé à l'arrestation d'Ajmi Lourimi. Ce dernier avait été interpellé à bord d'un véhicule dans la région de Borj El Amri, en compagnie d'un militant du mouvement Ennahdha faisant alors l'objet d'un avis de recherche au profit du Pôle judiciaire de lutte contre le terrorisme. Pour rappel Ajmi Lourimi est poursuivi pour « non-dénonciation aux autorités compétentes d'informations parvenues à sa connaissance concernant un crime terroriste » alors que Mossaâb Gharbi est accusé d'avoir fourni un lieu d'hébergement à une personne en lien avec des crimes terroristes et de l'avoir aidé à fuir. Y. N. L’article La Cour d’appel de Tunis rend son verdict dans l'affaire Lourimi & Gharbi est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.description: The letter “C” in APEC, stands for “Cooperation”, which is the focus of this year’s Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation meeting in southeastern China. items.title: Baisse de l’aide publique au développement: l’efficacité des programmes humanitaires évaluée
items.description: L’année dernière, l’aide publique au développement a baissé de 23 %, a documenté l’OCDE. Dans ce contexte, mesurer l’impact de l’aide humanitaire, afin de fournir des données probantes aux politiques et aux décideurs, est l’objectif principal du programme HPI de l’organisation J-Pal – des prix Nobel d’économie, les professeurs Abhijit Banerjee et Esther Duflo. Ce sont 22 programmes qui ont ainsi été évalués par des économistes de grandes universités afin de documenter rigoureusement l'impact (ou non) de ces programmes et financements.

items.title: La Tunisie devient le deuxième producteur mondial d'huile d'olive
items.description: La Tunisie prend la deuxième place au classement des producteurs d'huile d'olive, juste derrière l'Espagne. Les chiffres officiels le confirment, la récolte tunisienne a été exceptionnelle cette année : 500 000 tonnes, soit 50 % de plus que l'année dernière, et plus que la moyenne quinquennale de 320 000 tonnes. Cela fait des années que la Tunisie n'avait pas été aussi performante.

items.title: Madagascar: la région du Bongolava en proie aux feux de brousse
items.description: À Madagascar, le mois de novembre est marqué par une multiplication des feux dans les zones rurales, juste avant que ne débutent les pluies, soutenues et quotidiennes. Dans la région du Bongolava, à 200 kilomètres à l’ouest d’Antananarivo, les paysans utilisent le feu pour défricher les terres agricoles mais aussi pour renouveler les pâturages pour les zébus. Interdits par la loi mais tolérés dans la pratique, ces feux de brousse génèrent des conflits et dégradent durablement l’environnement.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI Is Really Weird
items.description: J ason Duval lives in a shack on the Leonida Keys, in the simulated Florida where Grand Theft Auto VI is set. I began playing the game after its release at midnight, and I have already tried and failed to outrun the police, roamed the hallways of a prison, driven a speedboat to collect cocaine dropped by a seaplane pilot who was skimming from a more upmarket criminal, and flown the seaplane to escape an RV park full of wild-animal-and-narcotics traffickers. If you know anything at all about the game, which almost 5,000 people worked on for more than a decade at a reported cost of more than $1 billion, it is that Leonida is enormous. Early reviewers are bragging on social media about spending more than 100 hours in the world of the game, while only scratching the surface of what is possible. The prospect seems overwhelming because I already have a life that requires labor and demands diversion, and I am worried about how to fit GTA VI ’s simulated work and recreation into my supposedly real life. Theorists of video games (a real thing that I could be accused of being) have a name for this phenomenon: playbor , a portmanteau of play and labor . Many jobs feel fake now anyway—“email jobs,” they were scornfully called even before AI could be mustered to carry out their pointlessness—and games feel like jobs, with a seemingly endless list of menial tasks for their players. [ Read: The least productive day of the year ] An hour or so in, though, the game offers a breather to look around and get your bearings. I decide to stay in Jason’s house instead of venturing out into even a tiny corner of Leonida. There is so much to do here that I find myself wondering how many hours I might spend indoors, inside the pretend home of a fake man. After all, I pass most of my own life as a real man inside my real home, working and puttering, instead of exploring the city or countryside that contain me. J ason has a pet snake, and walking by its glass habitat triggers a text overlay indicating that I can interact with it. I press a button to feed the snake, and Jason reaches into a blue plastic container, carefully retrieves a mouse, and drops it into the cage. I can see another mouse or two in there, of varied shades. I already feel as though I need to resupply the snake food. I find myself wondering where one goes for snake mice, and what that shop might be called in Grand Theft Auto . “Thoughtful actions will increase your focus bar,” the game tells me after I feed the animal. Feeding a snake is thoughtful, apparently. A purple icon animates and a corresponding purple bar fills slightly to communicate the effect of the act. Jason’s stamina and strength are also measured in health-bar form. Some games allocate a bar for hunger or even bladder level. This kind of thing used to seem ridiculous, a perverse way to understand human behavior for the nerds who design and play video games. But when I look at my real smartwatch on my actual wrist, I realize the world has caught up. It translates my movement into a number on a red bar that supposedly represents my activity. I don’t believe that the numbers—383 calories so far today—are real, but I orient my activities around them every day. Better do a quick Peloton to close my rings; time for another walk to get my steps in. I don’t think about it much anymore, but I have become a video-game avatar of myself. I n the shack, morning light pours across a desk from a window whose blinds are raised halfway. On the desk are a radio, a few books, and a conch shell. You know that a video-game object is relevant when it receives an overlay with a text description and an icon of the controller button used to interact with it. In this case, the radio’s channels can be changed with a button on my PlayStation 5 controller, and the book can be examined with a different button. I cannot interact with the conch. After flipping to a station called Afrobank FM, I examine the book. It’s called Orca: A Whole Different Animal . The book isn’t about killer whales. It’s a send-up of the Navy SEALs and the kind of inspirational title that a former officer might write as CEO of a private mercenary firm or in anticipation of running for a U.S. Senate seat. I can open the book, which contains actual text on simulated pages. I’ve read that Rockstar Games, the creator of GTA , did not use generative AI during the production of the game, and instead employs a large team of people who create all of the media inside it—including Orca , presumably. I wonder whether libraries or bookstores exist in the game, which I might then treat as a laborious literary experience rather than a criminal-underworld fantasy. But flipping through Orca reveals that the game surfaces only a few pages. The book is not real, in the sense that a book contains writing sufficient to justify a book. It is, instead, an icon of a book, like the conch is an icon for decor. I somewhat wish that Rockstar had used AI to generate books instead. I assume—I haven’t looked yet—that someone has, by now, generated a real, fake version of Orca: A Whole Different Animal and put it up for sale on Amazon. J ason’s eyes suggest an earnestness that makes me want to like him. The hairs at the top of the mustache stick out and up slightly, in a casual manner that suggests affability more than unkemptness. It seems remarkable to be able to interpret a character in this way, and I find myself suspicious of the matter. Not too long ago, an “uncanny valley” effect made computer characters seem unreal—they were immensely real but just shy of credible, and that gap made them slightly creepy. The gap appears to have been closed. Now, instead, I wonder whether I really like Jason or am being tricked into liking him by how well the game has established his plight. Earlier, he hooked up with Lucia Caminos, the game’s other protagonist, whom I had controlled as she committed a robbery that got her arrested. I’ve watched Jason tolerate a prolix conspiracy theorist named Cal and rescue a hot-mess smuggler named Donnie. His ex-military credentials have been established, and Jason’s all-American appearance suggests a good guy in a bad spot. The writing and characterization are good in the way a television show is these days—which is to say, too good, too clean. The paradox of fiction has become the new hurdle. I find myself worrying that my years of vocal skepticism about video-game storytelling are at risk of coming undone. W hen uncanniness persists, it offers me comfort. In the kitchen, I can make Jason pour a coffee and drink it. Doing so raises his focus and his stamina, as coffee is known to do. He drinks it so quickly that I worry about scalding him, but that is tempered by the realization that he didn’t really drink it—no liquid moves between the mug’s lip and Jason’s mouth, as if the mug had been a prop in a black-box theater production or a stop-motion animation. The simplest background acts of other narrative media, such as films or novels, require enormous amounts of engineering to accomplish in software. In a book, you can say, “Jason poured and drank a cup of coffee.” In a movie, you can point the camera at an actor doing so, and the act along with the liquid’s heat shimmer would be captured through the lens. But nothing is free in games. Jason continues holding the mug as I walk around his place. It dangles from his right hand like a cigarette. When he opens the fridge at the behest of a button press, he does so with his nonpreferred hand, so he can continue clinging to the mug. The game interprets the mug in the same way it would a pistol—an object is probably a weapon, one that you’d want to put down only deliberately. If I let go of the controller, Jason enters what game developers call an idle state. It would seem weird if a game simply stopped when the player isn’t doing something, so the software makes the characters bob and sway in a manner that seems realistic until it goes on too long. Jason’s body moves to the beat of the music on Afrobank FM, in this case “Tomorrow,” by Ntombi Ndaba, a real South African singer from the late 1980s. GTA often does this, mixing mocking or fictional media with licensed ones in a way that makes you doubt whether you know which element is real and which is invented. That feeling accompanies every moment of life today, because the internet is full of lies that might also be true. Idle Jason nodded his fictional head along to the real Ntombi Ndaba in his fictional Leonida tank top, as if to agree with me. S ome of my colleagues in writing and academia—the ones who hate artificial intelligence—have taken to the idea that “writing is thinking.” They use this shorthand as a self-evident takedown of AI. If people had to write (well, presumably?) to think, then nobody would ever think—especially academics. I have to walk to think, so I put down the PlayStation controller to take a walk to try to figure out what I think about Grand Theft Auto VI . After you have played a video game, the real world feels more akin to the apparatus you control in a video game. My feet no longer felt like my own as they crunched gravel on the street. Construction is everywhere in my neighborhood, the consequence of a tornado that blew through here 18 months ago. I steered my human body around a hole in the pavement and a construction dumpster at the gutter. A worker was standing between the sidewalk and an approaching pickup truck, and I had to veer uncomfortably close to him to get by. As I did, I inhaled the strong smell of his cologne, which vanished as quickly as it appeared. You cannot smell in Grand Theft Auto , a game for the eyes and ears and thumbs. This somehow made smelling seem unimportant, rather than making the game feel insufficiently realistic. The construction worker’s cologne came across as improbable and fake. A wardrobe in the corner allows me to change Jason out of his tank top and into other garments—a military outfit, workout wear, pajamas. I switch to swimwear, and the game previews Jason in red trunks and no shirt. I find myself studying his body in distressing detail. I’ve been working out seriously for the past two years or so and become occasionally concerned about the tone of my abs, a vanity I find embarrassing to admit. Along the way, I’ve worried that the AI depictions of the human body on YouTube fitness-video previews are giving me body dysmorphia. Jason’s abs look as toned (or less?) than mine, which I had checked in the mirror this morning. This fact makes me feel somehow affirmed—that I am in as good of shape as an animated video-game antihero. A triangle appears in Jason’s bathroom, indicating that I can shower. Doing so cuts to a shot of Jason from behind, his naked ass visible under the flowing water. Nudity feels like an attempt to make a video game serious in the way that it once did for cable-television shows. The whole idea has been prudishly outmoded on TV; there, visible vomiting indicates seriousness rather than butts or boobs. [ Ian Bogost: Zelda’s midlife crisis ] I can make Jason shower, after a fashion. You pull a trigger on the controller to scrub and, while doing so, use the left joystick to move his hands. Driving is like this too—akin to piloting a vehicle, if a vehicle were a marionette instead of a machine. Getting clean increases Jason’s focus. When he emerges from the shower (hold a button to dress), Jason is still carrying the coffee mug. Years ago, I took my son to the empty parking lot of a local shopping mall to teach him to drive. He struggled with hand-over-hand steering, because video games had given him a false idea about the process of driving a vehicle. Driving in video games has always overstated the sensitivity of steering. (A few years later, my daughter, who had played only Nintendo’s Animal Crossing , had no such trouble.) Jason drives a beat-up Chevy El Camino, which is fictionalized as the Cheval Picador in the series. Although GTA has always encouraged reckless driving, I had heard that you have to be more careful in this game, because you need to repair your car if it gets damaged, and that requires money, which demands in-game work. But the game frustrated my attempts to drive properly, as if the ghosts of its prior iterations were haunting the new doctrine of vehicular realism. Backing up has always been a freak show in GTA , and I immediately blew out a taillight. When I regained composure, I found myself commuting, for real. I kept two car lengths back in traffic. I stopped at stop signs in the middle of nowhere. I took turns wide and felt guilty when my perception of the road, unaided by the embodiment that would make real driving easy, caused me to mistake an oncoming lane for my own. When I arrived at Jason’s house, where the map had guided me, I accidentally pulled into a neighboring property. It was night and hard to see. I felt guilty, the way you do when your Uber from the airport pulls into a neighbor’s driveway instead of your own. Y ears ago, a less adept game with similarly adult ambitions, called Heavy Rain , allowed the player to intervene in narrative cutscenes via a technique known as quick-time events. Early on, the player loses track of a child named Jason in a mall. This failure turns tragic and motivates the rest of the story (which is, alas, stupid). The game instructs the player, who is frantically searching for Jason, to press “X” to call out for him. This mortifying depiction of human terror became a meme, at a time when memes were still new: “Press X to Jason.” Surely, it is no accident that one of the main characters in GTA VI is also named Jason. Pressing “X” to Jason has finally grown up, not because the act is more serious but because the world has acclimated to it. Press “X” to dinner in DoorDash. Press “X” to time off in Workday. Press “X” to health care in MyChart. Someone told me that they heard Grand Theft Auto VI begins with a lot of cutscenes. That is not quite right. It begins with paperwork. Accept the license agreement. Affirm the privacy policy. Choose your heads-up-display design. Calibrate the brightness and color gamut of your monitor. Enable subtitles or select on-screen-text size. Games such as this one have longed to meet or replace Hollywood films for decades. In some ways, they have. In others, the reverse has taken place. Watching television or cinema—which one does at home now, principally—involves operating software services as much as consuming media: scrolling menus, running updates, scanning QR codes to log in. T he French theorist Jean Baudrillard knew about the future—our present—decades before time revealed it to you and me. Everything would become simulation, a barrage of representation replacing lived reality. These were ideas, complex and hard-to-read ones. Baudrillard also anticipated the form of the internet age, with its short bursts of disconnected meaning. He wrote many books entirely from aphorisms, including one about America (called America ) and a series on anything he could think of (called Cool Memories ). Just as the photographer Stephen Shore accidentally invented Instagram in the 1970s, so Baudrillard accidentally invented Twitter in the 1980s. Two weeks ago, culling some of the many books in my office, I donated a couple boxes of ’80s and ’90s theory that felt irrelevant today. But I kept America and Cool Memories . I have always yearned to write like that, like Baudrillard, in aphorism rather than argument. GTA VI finally justified it, by turning life (or its simulation) into a series of disconnected rituals. I have to make a disclosure. Take-Two Interactive, the company that owns Rockstar Games, the creator of GTA VI , has paid me a lot of money over the years for legal consulting related to intellectual-property litigation. One of those cases involved the parent company’s sports games, such as the NBA 2K series, made by the Take-Two subsidiary 2K Games. A tattoo artist had sued Take-Two for reproducing the tattoos he had inked on LeBron James’s actual body, which he claimed the game developer needed permission to reproduce in virtual form, despite the fact that 2K Games had secured the rights to James’s (and every other NBA player’s) likeness via an agreement with the NBA. The realism of the games was central to the dispute. [ Listen: Will the new Grand Theft Auto be a weapon in the culture wars? ] During the trial’s testimony, the opposing counsel showed me a version of NBA 2K that his litigation team had configured to play with two teams composed entirely of LeBron Jameses. “Is this realistic?” the attorney challenged. “Yes,” I responded. What he showed amounted to a realistic depiction of what reality would look like were you to stage a professional basketball game composed entirely of James clones. Take-Two won the case . O ut on Jason’s deck, ring marks on the wooden railing caps look like they have been painted on rather than worn in as moisture. When I look across the swampy bog surrounding the house, everything is too bright. The shadows don’t look dark enough, and the highlights appear too washed out. It looks like a high-dynamic-range computer rendering. Or it did, before the software in smartphones, which are the devices people now use to take photographs, started performing intensive processing, including high dynamic range. That’s why what you see in the world tends to look deep-fried in your pictures. That style is now so commonplace that it has become what a photograph looks like—what the world looks like, once it is shared as photographs on social media. There, looking across the HDR water of the Leonida Keys, I held a button on the controller to put down the mug Jason was still holding. He set it on the wood railing cap overlooking the swamp. There, the software gave it a label, Mug , and a triangle icon indicating that I could pick it up again.

items.title: Traqué pour escroquerie et blanchiment : L’enseignant Ramdé Yamlanéba interpellé 3 heures après l’avis de recherche
items.description: Recherché pour des faits présumés d'escroquerie, d'abus de confiance et de blanchiment de capitaux portant sur une importante somme d'argent, l'enseignant Ramdé Yamlanéba a été appréhendé le jeudi 19 novembre 2026 à Koudougou. Rattrapé seulement trois heures environ après la diffusion d'un avis de recherche par la Police Nationale sur sa page Facebook, le suspect tentait d'échapper aux forces de l'ordre après avoir été aperçu à Tampouy. Cette interpellation record illustre l'efficacité de la collaboration entre la Police Nationale, la Police Municipale de Koudougou, les Forces de Défense et de Sécurité (FDS) et la population. La traque aura été d'une rapidité inédite. Ce jeudi 19 novembre 2026, la Police Nationale du Burkina Faso a publié sur sa page Facebook un avis de recherche ciblant Ramdé Yamlanéba (également orthographié Yamlénéba). Né le 17 juillet 1968 à Imasgo dans la province du Boulkiemdé, cet enseignant de profession, domicilié au quartier Tampouy à Ouagadougou, faisait l'objet de recherches actives pour des faits présumés d'escroquerie, d'abus de confiance et de blanchiment de capitaux portant sur une importante somme d'argent. Les services de sécurité avaient également signalé que l'intéressé avait été aperçu à Tampouy et manifestait l'intention de quitter le territoire national, incitant les autorités à lancer un appel pressant à la vigilance citoyenne. La mobilisation générale n'a pas tardé à porter ses fruits. Seulement trois heures environ après la publication officielle de l'avis de recherche, le suspect a été localisé et appréhendé à Koudougou, chef-lieu de la région de Nando. Cette arrestation éclair a été rendue possible grâce au concours précieux des citoyens et à une synergie d'action exemplaire entre les différentes composantes des Forces de Défense et de Sécurité (FDS), avec une mention particulière pour la Police Municipale de Koudougou. Cette opération victorieuse met en lumière la force de la coproduction de la sécurité. Dans son communiqué, la Police Nationale a réitéré sa profonde gratitude envers la Police Municipale de Koudougou pour son soutien inestimable, tout en saluant la promptitude et la collaboration exemplaire de la population. En sollicitant cette vigilance citoyenne pour stopper la criminalité financière et permettre la poursuite des procédures judiciaires, les forces de sécurité rappellent qu'une telle synergie est essentielle pour bouter l'insécurité hors des cités. items.title: La formation et la paix sociale au cœur d’un panel
items.description: Moustapha Diop, ancien directeur des ressources humaines de la RTS et ancien responsable syndical appelle aux jeunes de l'entreprise de presse à l'unité et à la quête du savoir. Il animait un panel organisé par l'amicale des jeunes de la RTS, à l'occasion de la journée d'intégration. La nouvelle équipe de l'amicale des jeunes de la RTS dirigée par la demoiselle Toumané Faye a tenu ce jeudi 19 novembre dans le hall de la RTS une journée d’intégration, une rencontre qui marque le démarrage officiel des activités de l'amicale des jeunes de la RTS. L'événement qui a mobilisé tous les travailleurs de l'entreprise a été un moment d'échange et de partage sur des questions relatives à la formation, à l’unité et la paix sociale. Dans sa communication le panéliste Moustapha Diop a fait un rappelle de l’historique et de la mission de la radiotélévision sénégalaise, avant d’insister sur la formation continue, l'humilité et la patience surtout des jeunes. « Le savoir est une ressource indispensable dans la vie de l'individu, et dans un monde en profondes mutations marquées par le numérique, le digital et l’intelligence artificielle, la connaissance devient plus qu'une arme » déclare Moustapha Diop, panéliste. Ce dernier a aussi invité les jeunes à se rapprocher des anciens de la maison pour pouvoir bénéficier de leur générosité. « Des anciens comme Omar Diao du journal télévisé, par ailleurs formateur au Cesti est une ressource sûre qui peut apporter beaucoup de choses dans le domaine de la formation, vous devez en profiter » conseille le panéliste. Dans leurs interventions, la directrice du capital humain de la RTS et Khaly Seck conseiller spécial du directeur général de la RTS ont rassuré les jeunes à propos de la formation. « La formation est un pilier fondamental dans toute entreprise et la RTS en est consciente. C'est dans ce cadre d'ailleurs que les autorités ont promis de relancer l'académie de la RTS pour prendre en charge ce volet » renseigne Khaly Seck. La nouvelle présidente de l'amicale des jeunes de la RTS, Toumané Faye a saisi l'occasion pour remercier la direction générale de la RTS, les cadres et tous ses collègues pour leur soutien et leurs conseils qui ont permis de réussir la journée. Pape. Coly NGOME

items.title: Agriculture: Madina Bah confirmée à la tête de la Direction Nationale du foncier rural et du patrimoine agricole
items.description: Madina Bah est officiellement confirmée à son poste de Directrice nationale du foncier rural et du patrimoine agricole. La décision a été actée ce jeudi 19 novembre 2026, à travers un décret lu à la télévision nationale. Sociologue de formation, Madina Bah avait été nommée à la tête de cette direction en juin 2023, après avoir occupé les fonctions de Directrice générale adjointe, chargée des finances et de l'administration, à la Société guinéenne de palmiers à huile et d'hévéas (SOGUIPAH). Son parcours professionnel est également marqué par une solide expérience au sein du système des Nations unies, notamment à l'UNICEF, où elle a occupé plusieurs responsabilités. De 2007 à juin 2018, elle a été Cheffe du bureau de zone ouest de l'UNICEF Guinée. Auparavant, de juin 2007 à août 2014, elle a exercé comme administratrice au programme Eau, hygiène et assainissement de cette institution. Plus récemment, de septembre à décembre 2020, elle est intervenue en qualité de consultante de l'UNICEF en appui à la mise en œuvre des projets PBF (Peace Building Fund). Avant ces différentes responsabilités au sein de l'UNICEF, Madina Bah avait dirigé le Centre régional pour l'eau potable et l'assainissement à faible coût (CREPA) en Guinée, en qualité de Directrice résidente, d'août 2001 à mai 2007. Sa confirmation à la tête de la Direction nationale du foncier rural et du patrimoine agricole s'inscrit dans la continuité des réformes entreprises au sein du département de l'Agriculture, en général, et dans le domaine du foncier agricole, en particulier. Elle poursuivra ainsi ses fonctions à la tête de cette structure, au cœur des enjeux liés à la gestion du foncier agricole en Guinée. items.title: Gamou de Pire : 95 % des besoins couverts, l’État vise une organisation réussie
items.description: Réunis autour du gouverneur de Thiès pour préparer l'édition 2026 du Gamou annuel de Pire, les services de l'État et le comité d'organisation affichent la même satisfaction : 95 à 96% des doléances exprimées sont prises en charge. Sécurité, eau, éclairage, santé, routes seront fin prêts, avec une réunion de coordination prévue le 26 novembre et une journée de nettoiement le 1er décembre. « Année après année, les problèmes se règlent dans le cadre de l'organisation du Gamou annuel de Pire, dans le département de Tivaouane ». C'est le sentiment général qui s'est dégagé de la réunion de préparation du Gamou annuel de Pire, tenue ce jeudi 19 novembre, sous la présidence du gouverneur de Thiès, en présence du préfet de Tivaouane, du sous-préfet de Pambal, du maire de Pire, des chefs de services et du comité d'organisation. Selon le Khalife de Pire, Mame Abdou Cissé, tous les problèmes qui se posaient auparavant avec acuité ont été réglés pour une bonne tenue de l'événement, prévu cette année le 5 décembre 2026. Selon lui, dès 2023, 95% des doléances étaient déjà satisfaites. Depuis, des avancées ont été enregistrées dans des domaines où Pire a été, dit-il, privilégiée. Pour lui, la réunion du jour n'est donc qu'une « réunion de routine institutionnelle », pour faire le point et améliorer l'existant. Le Khalife de Pire n'a pas manqué de saluer la disponibilité de l'État, qu'il attribue à la volonté du président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, qui accorde beaucoup d'importance aux foyers religieux a-t-il insisté, demandant au gouverneur d'être son interprète auprès du chef de l'État. Il a également salué la pose de la première pierre de la Maison des Hôtes de Pire, une très vieille revendication. Une annonce qui, lorsqu'elle a été faite par le maire, lors d'une cérémonie officielle du Gamou, avait suscité les applaudissements de toute l'assistance C'est un projet de grande envergure, de grand standing », a-t-il ajouté. Prenant la parole pour clore la réunion, le gouverneur adjoint, Ababacar Sadikh Niang, a dressé un bilan largement positif. Selon lui, 95 à 96% des expressions de besoin formulées par le comité d'organisation seront satisfaites. Au chapitre des engagements, une réunion de coordination avec les forces de défense et de sécurité (gendarmerie, sapeurs-pompiers, ASP) est proposée le jeudi 26 novembre 2026. Pour la santé et le commerce, les services régionaux du commerce et de la santé mettront à disposition les éléments nécessaires pour le contrôle de la qualité des produits alimentaires et le respect des prix. La Senelec prendra toutes les dispositions nécessaires pour assurer la fourniture d'électricité durant le Gamou. Une journée de nettoiement est prévue le mardi 1er décembre 2026, avec l'appui de la SONAGED, en collaboration avec le maire de Pire. Un appel a été lancé à toutes les populations de la commune pour prêter main-forte à la SONAGED et au maire. Une réunion d'évaluation, qui servira de bilan à mi-parcours, est prévue le mercredi 2 décembre 2026, pour vérifier si les engagements pris ont été respectés et procéder aux derniers ajustements. Ibrahima NDIAYE (Correspondant)

items.title: Sánchez y Feijóo no se miran porque no pueden ni verse
items.description: Pedro Sánchez y Alberto Núñez Feijóo no pueden ni verse. Literalmente. Se apreció muy claramente cuando, media hora antes del inicio del debate, entraron en el plató con la moderadora, María Casado , para posar para los fotógrafos. Después del apretón de manos más forzado de la historia y alguna sonrisa nerviosa, buscaron cualquier excusa para no dirigirse siquiera la mirada: hablando por turnos con la presentadora, señalando la pantalla gigante que tenían detrás, o el reloj, o el suelo... lo que fuera antes de tener que mirar al rival un minuto más de los 90 estipulados del cara a cara. En cuanto los fotógrafos se retiraron, se sentaron a la mesa de 2,5 metros —la distancia parecía mayor, sideral— a repasar sus fichas en un silencio sepulcral. Seguir leyendo

items.title: World Court Finds Myanmar Committed Rohingya Genocide
items.description: Click to expand Image People gather outside the International Court of Justice following the landmark ruling that found Myanmar responsible for genocide against the Rohingya, The Hague, November 19, 2026. © 2026 Human Rights Watch (The Hague) – The International Court of Justice’s (ICJ) landmark ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya is a historic milestone in their long quest for justice, Human Rights Watch said today. On November 19, 2026, the ICJ found Myanmar responsible for genocide against the Rohingya during the 2016-2017 “clearance operations,” carried out by Myanmar’s military. In the case brought by Gambia against Myanmar for alleged violations of the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide (Genocide Convention), the court ruled for Gambia, with a nine to six vote by the judges, that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. This is the first time that the ICJ found a country responsible for committing genocide. The court also found that Myanmar violated other obligations under the Genocide Convention, including the obligations to punish those responsible for genocide and to prevent genocide. The court’s ruling is final and cannot be appealed. “The landmark International Court of Justice ruling is long-awaited recognition of the suffering the Rohingya have endured from Myanmar’s military,” said Maria Elena Vignoli, senior international justice counsel at Human Rights Watch. “The ruling also provides a significant precedent for victims of genocide and other grave crimes across the world in their own search for justice.” In August 2017, Myanmar’s security forces began a sweeping campaign of massacres, rape, and arson against ethnic Rohingya in northern Rakhine State that forced more than 700,000 people to flee to neighboring Bangladesh. In November 2019, Gambia filed a case before the ICJ alleging that Myanmar’s atrocities against the Rohingya constitute genocide and violate the Genocide Convention. This was also the first time that a country without any direct connection to the alleged crimes used its membership in the Genocide Convention to bring a case before the ICJ. The ICJ is the principal judicial organ of the United Nations, adjudicating disputes between states and issuing advisory opinions on international law. It consists of 15 judges elected by the UN General Assembly and Security Council for nine-year terms. In its ruling, the ICJ found that the evidence before it established that Myanmar’s security forces, and other state organs, intentionally committed the genocidal acts of killing, causing serious bodily or mental harm, and imposing measures intended to prevent births against the Rohingya. Considering the totality of the evidence, the court concluded that Myanmar committed these acts with the requisite genocidal intent to destroy a substantial part of the Rohingya population of Myanmar. To reach this conclusion, it considered an array of relevant factors, including the general context, the selective targeting of the Rohingya, acts that violated the foundations of the Rohingya group, such as sexual violence and targeting children, and the systematic nature of Myanmar’s actions. Based on these factors, the court found that Myanmar’s genocidal intent was “the only reasonable inference” that could be drawn from the evidence before it. The judges rejected the possibility that other alternative intents, such as to carry out counterinsurgency operations or to forcibly displace the Rohingya, could reasonably explain Myanmar’s conduct. In light of its findings, the court ordered Myanmar to cease its ongoing violations of the Genocide Convention, including its failure to enact legislation to give effect to the convention and its failure to investigate, prosecute, and punish genocide. It found that Myanmar needs to provide assurances of non-repetition and is obliged to prevent similar violations in the future. The court also established that Gambia was entitled to seek reparations on behalf of Rohingya victims and ordered Myanmar to provide them. These include forms of restitution such as allowing and facilitating the safe, voluntary and dignified return of the Rohingya to their place of residence, and the reunification of displaced families. Whenever restitution is materially impossible, the court ordered Myanmar to provide reparations in the form of compensation. The court’s reasoning in this case is expected to have a profound impact on other pending cases before the ICJ regarding alleged violations of the Genocide Convention. This includes the case filed by South Africa against Israel in December 2023. Prior to the Myanmar judgment, US officials sought to pressure the ICJ and its judges with regard to the legal threshold for genocide. The US government has already sanctioned the International Criminal Court and several of its officials in an effort to shield senior US and Israeli officials from facing serious crimes charges before the court. In February 2021, following the November 2020 Myanmar elections won by Aung San Suu Kyi’s National League for Democracy, the then-commander-in-chief, Sr. Gen. Min Aung Hlaing, led a military coup that overthrew the civilian government. More than five years later, Myanmar’s military junta continues to commit war crimes and crimes against humanity throughout the country. Min Aung Hlaing installed himself as president through fraudulent elections in December 2025 and January 2026. In Rakhine State since late 2023, Rohingya civilians have been caught in the hostilities between the junta and ethnic Arakan Army forces. Both parties have carried out grave abuses, including extrajudicial killings, widespread arson, and unlawful recruitment. The Myanmar military continues to commit war crimes against the Rohingya and the crimes against humanity of apartheid, persecution, and deprivation of liberty. The Arakan Army, which now controls most of Rakhine State, has tightened repression of the Rohingya, including forced labor and arbitrary detention, and has committed grave violations of the laws of war amounting to war crimes. ICJ judgments are legally binding on the parties to the case. If one party considers that the other has failed to comply with the court’s ruling, it may turn to the Security Council, which can “make recommendations or decide upon measures to be taken to give effect to the judgment.” The Security Council has never acted upon this discretionary power. The UN General Assembly can galvanize political support to enforce ICJ judgments by adopting resolutions calling for compliance. Individual countries can also influence compliance through their bilateral engagement with the relevant party. Eleven countries that are parties to the Genocide Convention intervened in Gambia’s case on limited issues relating to the construction of the convention. The court’s interpretation of the convention on these issues becomes legally binding for them. The ICJ ruling is a clear reminder of the importance of independent judicial institutions in upholding international law, Human Rights Watch said. “Myanmar should swiftly comply with the World court’s judgment and end its oppression of the Rohingya,” Vignoli said. “Concerned governments should strongly support the Rohingya and promote justice for atrocities, press Myanmar’s junta to comply with the judgment, and ensure the safe and voluntary return of Rohingya refugees to Myanmar.”

items.title: Burkina Faso : Le Conseil des Ministres dissout le Syndicat des Pharmaciens
items.description: Réuni le jeudi 19 novembre 2026 sous la présidence du capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, le Conseil des ministres a adopté plusieurs décisions majeures touchant à la santé, aux mines, à l'organisation professionnelle et aux infrastructures économiques. Parmi les principales annonces figurent la dissolution du Syndicat des pharmaciens du Burkina Faso, la construction de quatre Centres hospitaliers régionaux universitaires pour un coût de 324 milliards FCFA et la relance de la mine de zinc de Perkoa. Le Conseil des ministres du Burkina Faso a tenu sa session hebdomadaire, le jeudi 19 novembre 2026, à Ouagadougou, sous la présidence du chef de l'État, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. À l'issue de cette rencontre gouvernementale, plusieurs décisions et orientations ont été annoncées dans différents secteurs stratégiques du pays. Les principaux dossiers examinés concernent notamment la dissolution du Syndicat des pharmaciens du Burkina Faso, le renforcement des infrastructures sanitaires, la reprise de l'exploitation de la mine de zinc de Perkoa et les préparatifs de la célébration du 11 décembre 2026. Syndicat des pharmaciens : le gouvernement prononce la dissolution Au titre du ministère de l'Administration territoriale et de la Mobilité, le Conseil des ministres a adopté un décret portant dissolution du Syndicat des pharmaciens du Burkina Faso. Selon le ministre de la Justice, Édasso Rodrigue Bayala, assurant l'intérim du ministre d'État chargé de l'Administration territoriale et de la Mobilité, cette décision est motivée par l'exercice d'activités jugées contraires aux statuts de l'organisation. Le ministre a toutefois tenu à préciser que cette dissolution ne remet aucunement en cause l'exercice de l'activité pharmaceutique au Burkina Faso. Santé : 324 milliards FCFA pour construire quatre CHR-U Le secteur de la santé figure également parmi les priorités examinées par le Conseil. Un décret a été adopté pour autoriser le recrutement de prestataires chargés de la construction et de l'équipement de quatre Centres hospitaliers régionaux universitaires (CHR-U). Cette opération constitue la première phase d'un programme portant sur la réalisation de neuf établissements annoncés par le chef de l'État. Selon le ministre de la Santé, Robert Lucien Jean-Claude Kargougou, les travaux du CHR-U de Fada N'Gourma devraient démarrer en décembre 2026. Ceux des établissements de Banfora, Kaya et Koudougou sont programmés au cours de l'année 2027. Le coût global de réalisation de ces quatre infrastructures sanitaires est estimé à 324 milliards FCFA. Par ailleurs, le Conseil a instruit le redimensionnement du Centre hospitalier régional de Dédougou, actuellement en construction. Cette révision vise à accroître ses capacités d'accueil et à intégrer un centre de radiothérapie afin de renforcer la prise en charge des patients, notamment ceux atteints de cancer. Mine de zinc de Perkoa : la relance annoncée avec 1 250 emplois attendus Autre décision importante : la relance de l'exploitation industrielle de la grande mine de zinc de Perkoa, située dans la commune de Réo, dans la province du Sanguié, région de Nando. À cet effet, le Conseil des ministres a adopté un décret portant octroi d'un permis d'exploitation industrielle de grande mine de zinc à la société SOPAMIB Perkoa SA. Pour le ministre de l'Énergie, des Mines et des Carrières, Yacouba Zabré Gouba, cette réattribution marque une nouvelle étape dans la reprise de la production minière dans la région. Les retombées financières annoncées sont également importantes. Selon le ministre, la mise en service de la mine devrait générer plus de 96 milliards FCFA au profit du budget de l'État. Sur le plan de l’emploi, le projet devrait permettre la création de 400 emplois directs et 850 emplois indirects, soit un total prévisionnel de 1 250 emplois. Projet RAAGA : 104 milliards FCFA pour trois marchés modernes Au titre de la Présidence du Faso, le Conseil a également adopté le projet RAAGA, inscrit dans le cadre de l'Initiative présidentielle pour le développement communautaire (IPDC). D'un coût global estimé à 104 milliards FCFA, financé sur le budget de l'État, le projet prévoit la construction de trois marchés modernes dans les villes de Ouagadougou et de Bobo-Dioulasso. Cette initiative vise à moderniser les infrastructures marchandes, à soutenir les activités économiques locales et à favoriser la création d’emplois, particulièrement au profit des jeunes et des femmes. 11-Décembre 2026 : une grande parade militaire annoncée à Ouagadougou Les préparatifs de la célébration de la fête nationale du 11 décembre 2026 ont également fait l'objet d'une communication orale au cours du Conseil des ministres. Placée sous le thème : « Révolution Progressiste Populaire au Burkina Faso : une consécration des résistances à la domination coloniale et à l'impérialisme », cette édition sera notamment marquée, dans la capitale, par une grande parade militaire. À travers ces différentes décisions, le Conseil des ministres du 19 novembre 2026 a abordé plusieurs chantiers liés aux infrastructures sanitaires, à l'exploitation minière, à l'organisation professionnelle et au développement économique, ainsi qu'aux préparatifs de la prochaine célébration de la fête nationale. items.title: I Baked My Way Through The Atlantic ’s Archives
items.description: This is an edition of Time-Travel Thursdays, a journey through The Atlantic ’s archives to contextualize the present. Sign up here. The most cherished recipes are usually the hardest to follow. They live on stained index cards and notes worn thin at the creases, in handwriting so faded you have to squint to read it. That handwriting belongs to a grandmother or a distant relative, and it was meant for someone who already knew the dish: Add a pinch of this, a teacup of that; bake until done . I’ve spent a lot of time in The Atlantic ’s archives, and I kept running into such recipes tucked into letters, essays, and memoirs, rarely where you’d expect them. I was curious to know whether they still work—and, more important, how they taste. The further back I went, the less my finds looked like recipes. They read like stories, and you had to read closely to find the instructions. Take this “ Letter to a Young Housekeeper ,” from November 1865, written by C. P. Hawes to “M.,” a bride newly married to “H.” Hawes spends most of the letter arguing that cooking is a fine art and a science, which the woman of the house should learn for herself. She is funny about it, and a little grand. Recalling one early success at the table, Hawes reaches for Henry David Thoreau, whose essays had recently run in this magazine, to describe the dishes: “We ate, lingered, and revelled in them, thus becoming epicures at once … They were as great a revelation to the palate as Bettine or Thoreau might be to the mind.” Only at the very end does she mention a “well-tested” recipe for bread: a quart of milk, a teacup of “hopyeast,” and enough flour “to make it quite stiff.” How much flour? How hot an oven? And how long does it bake for? Hawes doesn’t say. For much of history, recipes moved from one cook to another by word of mouth and by experience: watching a mother at the stove, having a neighbor ask for a missing ingredient. Cookbooks didn’t exist simply because, for centuries, most women couldn’t read, Sarah Lohman, a culinary historian, told me. As literacy spread in the 18th century, women began keeping handwritten notes of family recipes to pass down or to copy for a daughter when she was married. Those recipes were light on instructions by design. They expected you to rely on your instincts “to know when the batter looks right or to know when the cake is done,” Lohman said. By the early 20th century, written recipes had become something to amass, and cookbooks were treated as literature. “It was with something of a shock that I woke one morning and found myself a collector of cookery books,” the American writer Elizabeth Robins Pennell wrote in The Atlantic in 1901. What she prized most were the traces that earlier owners of the books left behind. Her copy of The Queen-Like Closet , a 17th-century cookbook by Hannah Woolley, had several owners before it reached her—one of whom was a young woman named Mary Halfpenny, who had received it as a gift in 1678 and went on to add her own recipes to its pages. A century later, another family used it as their “Bible,” recording their children’s births in the margins. Pennell loved those scribbles: “They add a distinctly personal charm to the shabby little old cookery book.” And sometimes, the actual Bible held recipes too. In 1910, a writer in this magazine’s Contributors’ Club described the family Bible as a place where you might find anything tucked between the pages, from a father’s old report cards “to mother’s recipe for sponge-cake.” But around midcentury, the American recipe changed shape, in part due to technology. I asked Lohman why some of the 19th-century recipes I’d baked didn’t call for butter or eggs. Before the advent of the refrigerator, Lohman explained, these ingredients were seasonal: Cows give milk after calving, from late winter into summer, and hens tend to take a break from laying in winter. Sure enough, the 19th-century recipes missing those ingredients were fall and winter dishes. By the mid-1950s, the majority of American homes had a refrigerator. As kitchens changed, recipes changed with them: more exact, more complete, easier for a stranger to follow. But the story behind the food has never quite gone away. Even as recipes grew more precise and the ingredients in them stopped shifting with the seasons, the people who wrote them kept reaching for memories. In 1985, Corby Kummer, then an editor at The Atlantic , began an essay on pie not with flour or butter but with a tale about his mother’s pie crust, an unforgettable taste that “has driven me to pursue the elusive art of making pastry.” And as recipes moved online, the stories came with them. Food blogs, and later videos, wrapped their instructions in anecdotes; anyone who has looked up a recipe on their phone knows the feeling of scrolling past several paragraphs of backstory before the ingredient list appears. Some of that is less sentimental than it seems (long blocks of text help a recipe rank higher in search results and make more room for ads). Still, it is telling that when food writers have space to fill, they fill it with stories. I have been baking since I was a child, learning from my mother and grandmothers and from recipes handed down for generations. I was curious whether the recipes I found from over the decades still hold up today. So I baked my way through the archives, beginning with Hawes’s 1865 biscuits and ending on a batch of brownies from 2010. Where an ingredient or instruction was missing, I filled in what I thought each recipe left out and made my best guess about certain directions (what it means to age in a tin, or to roll to “exactly the right thickness”). The recipes below are adapted from the originals, based on my own testing (I’ve indicated any discrepancies with the original recipes by adding “modified” to the ingredients list). Here’s what happened—and my honest assessment of how it all tasted. Biscuits, 1865 In C. P. Hawes’s Atlantic story , she promises her dough will make “two small loaves and a half-dozen biscuits.” What came out of my oven were plain dinner rolls, and only about a dozen (there was no dough left for the loaves). Today’s biscuits are made with butter; Hawes’s dough is mostly milk, flour, and yeast. And not the yeast we buy now. Home bakers used to make their own, often by brewing it with hops. Hawes calls for a teacup of this so-called hop yeast—I used a packet of active dry yeast instead. The result: a simple bread roll with a slightly floury taste. Not quite a Thoreau-level revelation. But if you want a very simple dinner roll for the table, this is the recipe for you. (And if you’re after a tall, fluffy biscuit, Amanda Mull cracked the code in 2018.) Apple Dowdy, 1936 The cook and writer Della T. Lutes, whose Atlantic essays became part of her award-winning 1936 book, The Country Kitchen , calls her Apple Dowdy “a homely dish,” and she wasn’t being modest. A cross between an apple pie and an apple cobbler, mine came out of the oven looking exactly as advertised. At first, I wondered whether the Dowdy came before the pie, but not quite: Sarah Lohman told me that by the end of the 18th century, pies were “pretty much how they are today.” The pandowdy is just a less fussy way to get to a similar place. Lutes gives no quantities at all—she just writes that the dish needs a deep bed of sliced, spiced, buttered apples under a thick crust, baked “at least an hour, very slowly.” The result: a slightly watery dessert that isn’t the prettiest, but tastes decent. The consistency of the filling needed improvement, and it also could have used more flavor (I’d recommend going heavier on the spice). Lebkuchen, 1949 In 1949, the cookbook author Virginia Pasley described a holiday tradition that began with a search. Her mother “tried recipe after recipe” for Lebkuchen, a spiced German honey cookie, “like Mother used to make.” The Lebkuchen that finally passed the test came from Mrs. Schmidt next door. The writer and her siblings, who wanted to help, were allowed only to sliver the almonds and cut up the citron. Now I understand why. The recipe calls for so much honey that it ended up all over my kitchen, and stirring the stiff dough with 9(!) cups of flour was an arm workout. The result: This one was divisive among my taste-testers. The Lebkuchen is dense and very chewy, a workout for your jaw too. But if you like something not too sweet or soft to dunk in tea, this could be your cookie. Apple pie, 1985 and 2009 For this one, I paired two recipes from two eras. The crust comes from Corby Kummer , who opens his 1985 essay dismissing store-bought crust as tasting “like the box it came in.” His own recipe is the opposite: flaky, rich, and well worth the effort. The filling is from Ezekiel Emanuel’s 2009 apple-crisp recipe , which was helpful enough to provide me with a list of ingredients, a pan size, and the oven temperature. Pie crust Apple crisp filling The result: Kummer’s crust was so good that it stood out to the people who tried it. (Store-bought just doesn’t compare to his recipe.) The filling was a big step up from Lutes’s Dowdy. Emanuel himself says his filling is “almost identical to the one for apple pie,” and that’s how it tasted: like a solid, classic apple pie. Overall, a satisfying combination of recipes. Brownies, 2010 The newest recipe on my list comes from my colleague Eleanor Barkhorn, a senior editor at The Atlantic . It was part of a weekly series she wrote while training for a marathon. Unlike the older recipes, it leaves almost nothing to the imagination: There are eight ingredients and exact measurements. When I reached out to Eleanor, she had a few updates to the instructions: She sometimes ups the chocolate to 10 ounces, and she no longer recommends the mixer, because it can overmix the batter. Instead, she said it’s better to sift the flour onto the batter and then fold it in carefully with a spatula. The result: very good brownies with a perfect texture that were not hard to make. They were a favorite with my tasters. Definitely worth baking a batch. PS Family recipes are still finding their way into the pages of The Atlantic . For the December issue, Danyel Smith wrote about her Aunt Louise’s famous mac and cheese and the unexpected ingredient that set it apart. Does your family have a recipe like that, with a secret, a story, and one person who makes it best? I’d love to hear about it. Let us know in the comments. (We may share your answer, including your first name and last initial, age, and/or location, with fellow readers in a future edition of this newsletter or on our website or social-media platforms.) — Rafaela

items.title: Mentiras y medias verdades del debate cara a cara entre Pedro Sánchez y Alberto Núñez Feijóo
items.description: Vivienda Feijóo: “Prometió 184.000 viviendas, ¿sabe cuántas ha entregado, según la página web de La Moncloa? 540, el 0,29%” Seguir leyendo Sánchez: “Hemos rehabilitado más de medio millón de viviendas durante estos ocho años” Feijóo: “¿Sabe usted cuánto ha bajado la oferta de pisos en alquiler en Barcelona? El 69%. ¿Sabe usted cuánto han subido los desahucios en Barcelona? Tres veces más que en Madrid” Sánchez: “Cualquier vecino o vecina de la ciudad de Madrid o Valencia donde no se aplica la ley estatal de vivienda, si se aplicara se estarían ahorrando 500 euros al mes” Feijóo: “¿Sabe usted cuánto suponen los apartamentos turísticos en el total de viviendas? El 1%” Sánchez: “Hemos construido durante estos últimos ocho años un millón de viviendas de las cuales el 13% son protegidas” Feijóo: “Usted ha subido 100 veces los impuestos, 220.000 millones más de recaudación” Feijóo: “Por cierto, los 80.000 millones de fondos del Next Generation los tenemos que devolver, señor Sánchez. Los que usted ha gastado” Feijóo: “Le voy a dar el dato del salario medio neto ¿Sabe usted que ha perdido el poder adquisitivo del 3,8%?” Feijóo: “¿Por qué dice su portavoz que está a punto de petar el sistema de pensiones?”, pregunta Sánchez. “Pero si lo ha dicho el vicepresidente Cuerpo, en OndaCero con Rafa Latorre, lo tengo grabado”, le responde Feijóo. Sánchez: “Yo como presidente del Gobierno he subido al pensionista de 2018 a 2026 6.000 euros la pensión al año” Feijóo: “¿Cómo es posible que las pulseras antimaltrato no funcionen y que además usted esté siendo investigado por la Fiscalía Europea?” Feijóo: “Usted ha descarcelado [sic] a 1.400 violadores y gentes que han cometido abusos sexuales por su disparate de la ‘ley de solo el sí es sí“ Sánchez: “El 60% de la electricidad proviene de las energías renovables en nuestro país. El precio del MWh es un 27% más bajo que el promedio de la UE, mientras que en 2018 fue un 14% más alto” Sánchez: “Nos hemos propuesto, como además ya hemos asumido, el blindaje de la inversión en mantenimiento en seguridad de la alta velocidad por 19.000 euros millones durante los próximos seis años” Feijóo: “¿Sabe lo que hizo dos días después del funeral de Estado al que no acudió? Irse a un mitin y ponerse a bailar” Feijóo: “Cuando en un país se incrementan los descarrilamientos un 50% y cuando usted tiene el récord de gestión, el 70% de los muertos en alta velocidad en el mundo es suyo, debería ser usted un poco más prudente” Feijóo: “Por eso está usted imputado por financiación irregular en dos sumarios” Feijóo sobre el rechazo del PP al Tratado de Amistad con Francia: “¿Sabe usted por qué? Porque no se prevén las interconexiones eléctricas” Feijóo, al reprocharle Sánchez que quiere subir el gasto en defensa al 5% del PIB, responde: “Eso lo ha dicho usted y lo ha firmado usted en la OTAN” Feijóo: “España es el país con mayor pobreza infantil” Con información de: Guillermo Abril, Bárbara Ayuso, Belén Carreño, Gregorio Belinchón, Clemente Álvarez, Daniel Cordero, Irene Dorta, Javier F. Pérez, Emilio Sánchez Hidalgo, Elisa Silió, Carlos Torralba e Isabel Valdés.
